chapters.title: Chapter 1369 Silent Forts
paragraphs: Ravenshade Palace stood tall beneath a gray sky with its masterfully constructed spires rising like watchful silhouettes above the capital. The wards etched into its walls hummed with steady power, unchallenged for millennia. Inside, the atmosphere was controlled and restrained.

Tharion Ravenshade stood near the long table in his private strategy chamber with a thin crystal slate resting in his hand. Lines of sigils scrolled slowly across its surface as he reviewed the latest field report.
One of his most loyal and accomplished generals, who was trusted with 50,000 Ravenshade soldiers and ordered to help bring the end of the Vesper Consortium, had written it plainly, without flourish.

The army had linked up successfully with Tharion's sister, Queen Morgana, and her Elite Guards. Alongside the queen came the Scarlet Lilies, the five, well, four now due to Scar's death, Adamantite adventurers led by Lilith Ravenshade herself, Tharion's other sister. Furthermore, the Fujimori hit squad joined as well, consisting of some of the Silverwind duchy's finest, led by Lady Kaede herself.
Together with the Ravenshade army, they had begun the siege of Vesper Consortium strongholds, as Tharion ordered.
His eyes moved steadily across the text.
No notable resistance encountered.
No delays.
No casualties worth reporting.

Barriers had fallen under coordinated pressure. Morgana's brutal elemental firepower, Lilith's precision, and Kaede's unnervingly eerie strikes, still a mystery that Tharion desired to understand properly, overlapped cleanly. The report noted, almost as an aside, that not a single cannon had been fired so far, such was the might of the ladies and their allies.
Before they could prepare the cannons for a siege, it was already over.
Three fortresses had already fallen.
Tharion lowered the slate and allowed himself a small, contained smile.

"Good," he said quietly. "If my two unhinged sisters and that slit-eyed freak can all work to assist me instead of giving me constant headaches as they always do, it's time for us to bring out the champagne. I'll have to celebrate this once-in-a-lifetime occasion."
The duke seemed very content.
The Consortium had overreached. "I don't know what their plan was... I heard they went looking for allies in the Beastkin Confederation, but they're nowhere to be seen..."

Then his advisor spoke up. "They couldn't predict Alexios' power play to bring about this competition for the entire Greenvale Duchy. Without that, there would be no Fujimori or Ravenshade army to worry about. Furthermore, it was questionable whether Alexios would've made a move at all. There's a good chance he would've only ordered Alastair to take care of his own lands and left it at that. At least, until the syndicate began taking land. But I'm not sure if that was ever among their plans."
"Hmm... I suppose that's true. They drew the short end of the stick. Too many things they couldn't predict happened, turning their odds from acceptable to nightmarish," Tharion nodded.
But, well, it didn't matter if this current situation was the end result of dumb arrogance or sheer lack of luck; what mattered was the outcome, which was grim to say the least.

Then the duke's nonchalant expression turned to one of satisfaction. With this invasion, his obligation to Alexios would be fulfilled to the letter. The agreement had been clear. Support the crown against the Consortium, and Ravenshade would be rewarded.
There was more to be celebrating, however.

Alastair's incompetence had finally caught up to him. Now, the whole world knew of it, not just Tharion himself. Seeing the cost his old rival had to pay for his centuries of negligence, and that of his ancestors, filled the Ravenshade Duke with the sort of happiness no woman could ever provide him with.

The king's trust in that muscle-brained, arrogant mutt was gone. Alastair's standing among the other dukes had eroded. Even his image of strength before his own vassals had cracked. Once seen as an almighty ruler, who single-handedly defended the Vraven Kingdom against the might of the Beastman Confederation, now people could see him having to shamelessly fight for the mere right of being allowed to rule his own lands again.

Alexios had shown him the biggest disrespect a duke has ever received in the history of the kingdom, and it would not be forgotten. Tharion would make sure of that. He already hired numerous chroniclers to ensure history was recorded properly, as it should be.
Tharion turned the slate over in his hand once before setting it down. His expression returned to that of professional governor mode.

"Soon, Ravenshade will stand alone at the top. I will be the one to rule Vraven. Who knew that instead of amassing armies of overwhelming might, diplomacy and intrigue would get me so much farther in life? My ancestors were wrong in their approach."
He shook his head fondly as the thought settled comfortably.
Everything was moving as planned.
That was when the report arrived.
A courier knelt at the edge of the chamber, breath still uneven from haste. The sigil on his cloak marked him as internal intelligence.
The duke remained where he was, not even looking over his shoulder to look at the man as he ordered,
"Speak."
"Yes, My Lord! We lost contact with the border fortresses alongside Elvardian lands," the courier replied.
A pause came. Tharion finally turned around.
"How many?"
"Ten," came the answer. "Simultaneously."
The chamber did not erupt into panic or screaming.
Tharion walked over to his seat and leaned back.

At his side, the old man who was his sole trusted advisor, shifted his weight. The soft scrape of his staff against marble flooring was the only sound. His back was bent, his beard white, his eyes still clear.
Tharion turned his head a fraction. "What do you think?"
Halric took his time before answering. "The least troubling possibility is an artifact failure. Though ten synchronization arrays failing at once strains belief."
Tharion did not respond.

"Another option," Halric continued, "is internal unrest. Border towns seeking autonomy. With the resources poured into their defenses over the centuries, some may believe themselves capable of standing alone. That we would decide that it was more trouble than worth to siege our own lands."
Tharion lifted a hand, stopping him.
"I didn't ask you to invent theories you don't believe in. We've known each other too long for that. Stop skirting around like this and say what you think."
Halric's mouth curved. "Fair enough."
"This smells of an invasion," Tharion declared.
Halric nodded once. "You're right."

The old man's grip tightened slightly on his staff. "What troubles me is the silence before it. No troop movements. No supply strain. No buildup we could track. History tells us Elvardia never moves without leaving ripples. This time, there were none."

"Which leaves two real options," Halric went on. "The Covenant of Eternity has decided to show its hand, taking advantage of the Vesper Consortium drawing every eye elsewhere. They might've assumed it was time to use the chaos to their advantage, letting them achieve whatever unholy ambitions their dusty bones might desire."
"Hmm... It's possible. Damn it!" Tharion cursed. "If they turned ten whole settlements into their graveyards, breeding those filthy abominations of theirs, we'll have so many to cull."

"Yes, but I don't believe them to be strong enough to overtake ten strong settlements at once," Halric countered. "The most likely answer is that it's Elvardia again. Another test, like their failed push into our lands months ago."
Tharion nodded slowly, fingers brushing his chin as he considered it. "Maybe so. But this time, they're a lot more invested. The last invasion was a joke compared to making ten fortresses go silent."
"Perhaps the dwarves invented a suppressant artifact. They could be fighting a defensive siege as we speak," the advisor guessed.
"All this theorizing will only get us so far," Tharion decreed and stood.
"We have to organize a force and get to the bottom of this."

chapters.title: Chapter 1370 Senile King
paragraphs: Valorian's royal palace did not display that same level of calm and confidence that Ravenshade had.
King Alexios rose from his throne the moment the report was delivered.
"Say it again," he ordered.
The courier swallowed. "We lost contact with ten border fortresses, Your Majesty. All along the Elvardian frontier. The silence began at the same time."
The throne room quieted.
Alexios's expression turned grave instantly. Ten. Not one. Not two. Ten fortresses did not vanish because of storms, faulty arrays, or clerical failure.
He turned away from the court, steps measured as he walked down the raised dais. His mind was already elsewhere.
A memory surfaced, unwanted and sharp.
A call.
A familiar voice.
A tone that carried far too little respect.

"We might be criminal and king, a wanted man and the man who posts the bounties, but I still think of you in a favorable light," Quinlan had said. "You're a good man. I pity you for having been blessed by the worst wife known to mankind. So I just wanted to let you know that maybe you should strengthen-"
Then came silence in the call.
It was not a clean end of a sentence, nor was it the result of interruption by static. Quinlan merely paused before he finished his statement.
Alexios remembered leaning forward on his throne, irritation rising. "Strengthen what? Spit it out already. And stop badmouthing my damned wife."
Quinlan had remained silent for too long, as if paying attention to something else.
When he spoke again, the tone had shifted. It turned joking and arrogant.
"Strengthen your resolve to call me your emperor in the near future."
At the time, Alexios had seen only insolence. The man who was already the biggest pain in his behind was, once again, as he often did, posturing beyond his station.
Now, standing in his throne room with ten fortresses gone dark, the memory sat differently.
Alexios stopped walking.
His jaw tightened.
Quinlan had not finished his sentence the first time. He had stopped himself. Changed course. Whatever he had intended to say had been replaced with arrogance once he decided on something else.

This, combined with the fact that Alexios finally secured a rare victory when Quinlan had been repelled by the human city's barriers, hastily prepared under his direct orders. He was unable to repeat what he did in Greenvale, unable to force entry and claim more noble lives.
Then this happened.
Ten cities.
Along Elvardia's border.
All at once.
Alexios spun back toward the throne.
"That motherless heathen is at it again!" he roared.
The words cracked through the chamber, bouncing off marble and steel. Several advisors flinched outright.

"He is behind this. I am certain of it!" Alexios continued, voice rising. The old king was getting very animated as he shouted, "I want my orders delivered to Tharion immediately: SEND THE ARMY! I want whatever the Primordial Villain is doing brought to an end right now!"
A few of the older nobles exchanged looks. Not defiant ones per se, more so the kind reserved for moments when a figure in their community finally lost his battle against time and had gone senile.
Alexios saw it.
The hesitation. The sidelong glances. The careful silence.
For a breath, his mouth opened again, heat climbing his throat.
I am not crazy!
The words pressed against his teeth.
He forced them down.
His shoulders squared instead.
"My liege," one advisor said carefully, stepping forward with hands clasped. "By 'the army,' what scale do you intend? What should I tell Lord Tharion?"
Alexios turned on him.
"What scale?" he repeated.
The advisor hesitated. "Yes, Your Majesty. How many soldiers should be mobilized?"
Alexios did not hesitate.
"EVERY SINGLE ONE OF THEM!"
The room stiffened.
"Every banner. Every levy. Every knight sworn to this crown. Quinlan Elysiar must be stopped at any cost, or the cost will become our very lives in the near future."
Silence followed, thick and heavy. One advisor bowed deeply and hurried from the chamber to carry the order. Those who remained composed themselves, faces smooth, spines straight.
Too smooth.
Alexios saw it anyway. The lack of urgency. To them, Quinlan remained a problem someone else would solve. A nuisance that would solve itself with time. His luck would run out soon.
They were wrong.
That man was not a nuisance. He was the single most dangerous variable Alexios had faced in a thousand years.

An Elvardian invasion would not have made him blink. A beastkin horde would have earned a measured response. Criminal syndicates crawling out of the shadows was a development he used for political gains.
This was different.
This was a man who had risen from nothing.
Alexios looked over his vassals.
"I am an old man. My time on this plane is limited. Soon, I will earn the right to greet the Goddess."
A few heads dipped respectfully.
"But I refuse to leave my kingdom in worse shape than when my father placed this crown upon my head."

"My king," a noble spoke, cautious but sincere. "It is a worthy goal. But are you not placing too much weight on Quinlan Elysiar? We do not even know if he is involved. For all we know, he is busy planning his next move elsewhere."

Another voice followed. "Or perhaps he has already done all the damage he can behind enemy lines. Now that we stopped him in our cities, he may simply join the Consortium openly and become just another enemy to be met on the battlefield."
Several others nodded, polite and restrained toward the king, but in clear agreement that he was overreacting.
Alexios turned away from them. His gaze lifted to the statue of the Goddess at the far end of the hall. Stone eyes looked back, calm and distant.
"Grant me strength..."
He turned back slowly.
"You think this ends because we raised barriers. You think that because we denied him entry once, he will retreat."
His fingers curled against his palm.
"You do not understand what he is."
The room stayed quiet.
"We repelled his advance, yes," Alexios continued. "But ask yourselves this. Is that truly all he is capable of?"
He took a step forward.

"He is an elemental mage and a frontline warrior in one, casting large-scale, devastating spells while having the build to conduct hand-to-hand duels with strong warriors. He teleports. He commands necromantic forces that surpass anything our scholars have catalogued. Our first record of him is from this spring. This year. Before that, nothing. No family. No birthplace. No academy. No registry. He did not rise. He just appeared."
Murmurs stirred.

"We traced every archive we have. We found nothing. Then one day, the name Quinlan appears as the poor commoner boy who was lucky enough to be granted the right to purchase Ayame Fujimori as a slave. And within months, he goes from a presumed level one nobody who required a level fourteen samurai to survive goblin ambushes, to a man who turns the tides of war with his presence alone."
His voice sharpened.
"He forced an entire nation to scramble like blind men, reinforcing city barriers in panic, spending immense resources in the process. That was our response. Reaction. Not control."
Alexios's breathing grew heavier.
"And now you tell me he is done."
His hand struck the air.
"No. He is not done. Far from it. The Primordial Villain..."
The chamber stiffened.
"Is only getting started."
Many gulps sounded.
"I refuse to insult that horrible creature by believing he would be stopped so easily. That is why we respond properly. That is why we move with force and urgency."
He swept his gaze across every face.

"From this moment on, any matter involving Quinlan Elysiar is to be treated as a matter of national importance. No delays. No dismissals. No assumptions. Treat it as if our continued survival depended on it."
His voice echoed.
"Is that understood?"
No one spoke. Every advisor and noble present bowed.

chapters.title: Chapter 1371 Shocked Sentries
paragraphs: The wind howled.

Quinlan cut through the clouds at the front of the formation. Air folded around him in clean lines, not turbulence, not drag. The pressure bent outward as if the sky itself had learned how to move aside.

Behind him, the others flew in a tight cluster, held together by controlled currents that never quite touched the ground below. Rivers. Forests. Roads. All of it slid past in a blur of color and shadow before their eyes.
He concentrated and called upon even more.
The wind obeyed.
Ahead, the land soon darkened. Smoke traced thin lines into the sky. Siege towers. Barricades. Cannons. A city wrapped in tension and steel.
Quinlan's mouth curved.
"We've arrived."
He dropped.
The wind followed his intent, carrying the group down in a sharp arc before flaring outward at the last moment. They landed on a hill overlooking the battlefield.
Bows snapped up at once.

Elven archers occupied the hill, spread in disciplined lines between rocks and shallow trenches. The strategic importance of this high ground was recognized by Elvardia, and they'd sent a group to ensure the enemies didn't occupy it.
Because of that, drawn strings and gleaming arrowheads welcomed their arrival, already aligned with throats and chests.
"Halt!" one of them barked. "Identify yourselves!"

He tilted his head slightly. "Didn't they tell you? We've allied ourselves with Elvardia. I'm Quinlan Elysiar, and we already helped you people bring about the end of Greyhaven. We're here to do the same once again."

Despite his words, the archers did not lower their weapons. They looked a mere moment away from shooting, and the only thing that held them back was not Quinlan's reasoning but the cold eyes they were receiving from Sylvaris Vaelorith, an elf noble they recognized. She was not chained, not collared.
Her being here and supporting the scary-looking man made them pause.
"Hm?" Quinlan raised an eyebrow. Behind him, someone staggered.

Lucille swayed with one hand braced against her axe as her boots scraped the ground. Feng doubled over, dry retching, Felicity barely managing to turn away before doing the same. Ria, the blonde assassin girl who became their new friend, moved between them at once. She had one hand on each girl's back while even her own breathing was uneven.
Quinlan turned, frowning.
"...Huh? What's wrong?"
Ayame stepped up beside him.
"Quin," she spoke up with her eyes on the archers and hand on the hilt of her blade. "You're getting really powerful."
He blinked. "Of course I am? I just got a new level."
The oriental beauty shook her head. "I didn't mean it like that. You're becoming powerful not just because of levels."
She glanced back at the sky they had crossed. A faint hint of disbelief was written on her delicate features.
Serika, his tanned redhead who wielded solar powers, stepped up next to them. Just like Ayame, she was displaying hints of surprise. As another user of the flame, she noted her observation.

"Your level of control and depth is frankly getting scary, Quin. The explosion you created back in Greyhavn was more devastating than ever before, but that's only the beginning. As you said, you are gaining levels, so bigger explosions are to be expected. But... They were concentrated and controlled in a way I never saw you manage before. You compressed the flames until the detonation became so powerful that warriors who should've been able to take it with the combination of their high Vitality and defensive armor were overwhelmed as well. You killed a thousand trained soldiers in a single attack..."
She spoke the words with a face that was a mixture of sheer amazement and excitement, but also shock. Serika couldn't believe the mastery Quinlan was starting to display.

Vex nodded as she stepped up. Just like the other two, she wasn't shaken by the wind but by the badassness of her hubby. "The same happened with your wind!" she chirped while hugging his arm close to her chest with both hands. "You were flying so quickly that you outpaced the speed of command! Can you believe that? We crossed dozens of miles faster than the information arrived at the elven ladies."

The gorgeous Hexwitch's cheeks turned rosy as she spoke those words and squeeled like a schoolgirl who was overcome with how her crush stood out among the other boys during the PE exercises as the girls watched from the sidelines.
Understanding settled in Quinlan's mind.
"Oh."
Before he could say more, hurried footsteps sounded from below.
An elf sprinted up the hill, armor half-fastened, breath ragged. Sweat ran down her temples as she waved her arms.
"Pay attention, everyone! Command says a new allied force will arrive within minutes. Do not fire on a man falling from the sky surrounded by dozens of attractive women of mixed races-"
She stopped.
Her eyes locked onto Quinlan and the group behind him.
Her face drained of color.
"You're already here?!"
The wind tugged at Quinlan's coat as he smiled, slow and unapologetic, parting his arms wide. "What can I say? I am eager to help my favorite new allies."
The elf's eyes went wide.
Her mouth opened, then closed again as she straightened, forcing herself back into command posture. Behind him, several of the girls sighed.

Iris shook her head once, lips twitching despite herself. Feng wiped her mouth and muttered something under her breath. Felicity leaned against Ria, who rolled her eyes with practiced familiarity. Aurora pressed two fingers to her temple and exhaled slowly.
<So shameless!> All of them declared at once.
<Trying to help his new allies, he said!> Kitsara laughed.
<As if he had not just removed thousands of slaves from under Elvardia's nose. Slaves that would have filled their ranks, their workshops, their forges.> Lucille giggled.

<Slaves he will use to build his own nation that topples theirs in the future...> Jasmine added with incredible slyness present in her voice. The girl of humble merchant origins wasn't here in the flesh, as her arrangement with Quinlan was that she would oversee his lands while he fought with the rest of his wives at his side. She was his governor. However, she could send her forces at any moment if Quinlan asked for it and opened a portal from his location.
The elf knew none of these details, however.
She recovered quickly, planting her feet and giving him a firm nod. "Your eagerness is appreciated," she said, voice steady again. "I will inform my superiors of your early arrival."
Her gaze flicked to the group behind him. Then to the sky they had come from.

"My orders are to allow you to act at your own discretion." She turned and gestured toward the battlefield below, smoke drifting over siege lines and glowing runes flickering along the city's barrier. "Therefore, I will leave you to it, Lord Villain."
She bowed her head once, clean and respectful, then moved off the hill at a brisk pace.
Ayame didn't wait a single second.
"Lord Villain," she said with an amused chuckle leaving her lips.
Quinlan shrugged. "It certainly needs an acquired taste. But I think there's a nice ring to it."

Serika smiled, hearing the exchange between Quinlan and his cheeky samurai, but her attention was already on the siege. Her eyes narrowed slightly as she watched the barrier ripple under sustained fire. "That shield's about to fail. A few more minutes at most, I'd wager."
She glanced at him. "Should we do the same again?"
Quinlan shook his head. "No. That was a statement of power. 'We are here, and we are not nuisances.'"

He looked back at the field. "Not only was it dangerous, but you ladies don't regenerate mana the way I do. I want you to spend it on killing strong enemies, not cracking walls. We should let our allies show us that they, too, are worthy."
Many elven eyes narrowed at that. What kind of arrogance is needed to have such a train of thought? Their giant, powerful nation needed to prove that it was worthy of his time?
Serika nodded, clearly satisfied with his reasoning. "Then we watch?"
"Sure."
He stamped his foot once.

The ground shifted. Stone rose in clean, rectangular blocks, smoothing itself into thrones as if carved by an invisible hand. One by one, the girls took seats, settling in with varying degrees of comfort and curiosity, eyes fixed on the unfolding siege below.
The elven archers slowly lowered their bows.
Several of them stared.

A man had fallen from the sky. Claimed alliance. Been given permission to do whatever he pleased, despite the strictness with which their armies tended to operate. Then sat down to watch a city fall like it was a stage performance and had the balls to say he would not do anything because Elvardia had to prove itself worthy.
It was ridiculous. Plain ridiculous. Many eyebrows twitched.
Unconcerned with the opinion of others, Quinlan leaned back, resting his arms against the shoulders of the two closest wives who ended up sitting next to him.
The barrier flickered again.

She spoke the words with a face that was a mixture of sheer amazement and excitement, but also shock.
Serika couldn't believe the mastery Quinlan was starting to display.
Vex nodded as she stepped up.
Just like the other two, she wasn't shaken by the wind but by the badassness of her hubby.
"The same happened with your wind!" she chirped while hugging his arm close to her chest with both hands.
"You were flying so quickly that you outpaced the speed of command!
Can you believe that?
We crossed dozens of miles faster than the information arrived at the elven ladies."

The gorgeous Hexwitch's cheeks turned rosy as she spoke those words and squeeled like a schoolgirl who was overcome with how her crush stood out among the other boys during the PE exercises as the girls watched from the sidelines.
Understanding settled in Quinlan's mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 1372 Messing with the Fangirl
paragraphs: The barrier flickered again.

Dwarven artillery thundered from the siege lines below. Thick shells slammed into the glowing dome, each impact forcing ripples across its surface like water struck by a hammer. Runes flared, dimmed, then flared again.
Orianna leaned back in her earthen seat, one leg crossed over the other, eyes fixed on the spectacle below.
"You people certainly know how to live," she murmured lightly.

The pink-haired, tatted baddie rested her body after the battle of Greyhaven while watching cannons chew at the barrier as smoke rolled across the plains. For someone like her, sitting comfortably on a hill and observing a siege like a curated event was a whole new experience.

As she was a career criminal, Orianna tended to stay away from conflicts of this scale. And as the Consortium used to work in the shadows until they started their beef with Alastair, she never got to see a spectacle that came even close to what she witnessed on this day.
"I know, right?!" Ria gasped while leaning forward so fast she nearly slipped off her chair.
The blonde assassin's eyes sparkled as she stared at the battlefield, then flicked toward Quinlan. Her ears burned. "This is crazy... So crazy..." she murmured, more so to herself.
Iris barely glanced up, observing with a nonchalant expression. "You get used to it. This guy is just as arrogant as he is resourceful."

Ria snapped her head around. "Hah? Get used to THIS?! Never!" She pointed accusingly at her friend. "And, by the way, I can't believe you had an ally like him all along, and we spent months walking everywhere like peasants. We slept in dirty tents, and I did my business in... Anyhow!! I'm mad at you, Iris Ravenclaw! You're a bad woman. I won't call you my friend for at least ten minutes. Hmph!"
"Thank the Goddess. Finally, some peace and quiet."
Ria's eyes nearly popped out of their sockets. "Hey!!"
"I am not a transportation vessel, by the way," Quinlan said calmly.
Ria instantly yelped. "I-I didn't mean it like that!"
"Is that so?" Quinlan mused playfully.

The assassin shrank when she realized her words might be interpreted in a way she didn't mean them, making the girl twist in her seat. Feng and Felicity exchanged a look, then smirked in unison. The two young ladies were enjoying the misery this hopeless fangirl was putting herself into by interacting with Quinlan, who was clearly messing with her, enjoying the situation.
"I'm sorry," Ria blurted, cheeks red. "I really didn't mean to offend you."
Quinlan stood.
Stone shifted softly beneath his boots as he turned toward her, and a small smile tugged at his lips. "Relax. You don't have to walk around eggshells near me. I was just messing with you."
Ria's pout deepened. So did the crimson color in her face.

Blossom looked up at him with her tail wagging behind her butt. She was enjoying listening to the exchange between the ladies and Quinlan while watching the loud cannon fire beneath. Just as Quinlan predicted, the dogkin girl with far too acute senses got used to the loudness of dwarven cannon fire, letting her function normally. However, she was still uncomfortable around it, so much so that she had to fight back the urge to sabotage the horrible machines. 'Not yet, Blossom. You have to wait until Master decides to betray them or you'll ruin his genius plans!!' she reminded herself.
"Master!! Are you going somewhere?" Blossom asked, already half rising from her chair. Her tail swayed behind her without restraint. "Can Blossom come with?"
"Just a quick trip," Quinlan replied. "I'm missing someone. She should be here with us."
Blossom blinked. Her head tilted.
Quinlan smiled and parted his arms. "Sure. Come, Blossom."
That was all the permission she needed.

She sprang from her seat and straight into his waiting arms, light despite the leather and steel. Quinlan caught her easily. Her body pressed close without hesitation, and she giggled cutely, happily. "Hehe!"

The black leather she favored left little to the imagination. The gear hugged her hips and chest tightly, straps crossing skin more than they covered it. Beastkin favoring loose armor that let them feel more natural and thus effective was a hill Blossom was willing to die on. Quinlan gave up, deciding that instead of fighting her on the topic, he'd just enjoy the heavenly sight of his gorgeous lover in her BDSM-style gear.
Warmth bled through the contact. Her tail whipped back and forth as she buried her face against him, nuzzling without restraint. "Master..." she murmured, satisfied.
Synchra shifted.
The armor along Quinlan's chest flowed like liquid metal, parting just enough to expose skin where Blossom's head rested. A faint glow traced the edge of the transformation before settling.
Blossom noticed at once and began purring while nestling her head even closer.
"Thank you, Miss Synchra! You're amazing!"
A small lick of red flame flickered across the exposed metal in response, brief and precise.
Quinlan exhaled through his nose, amused. He could never get enough of his dog girl.
He looked up. "Liora. If you would."

The priestess stiffened when her name was called. She glanced between him and Blossom, then the realization set in. Her posture straightened. She nodded once and rose from her seat, hands already gathering light as she stepped closer.
Quinlan opened a hand. "[Warp Gate]."

Space folded inward, edges curling like peeled bark. A dark doorway split the air beside him, its surface reflecting nothing of the battlefield. "I'll be back before it falls," he said, already stepping forward.
Behind them, the others stayed seated, eyes returning to the barrier below as another volley of shells hammered into it.
Just before Quinlan crossed the threshold, voices rose.

Ayame leaned back in her chair with her arms folded. Anyone who knew the woman knew that the way her eyes sparkled and how her expression turned smug meant nothing good. "By the way, Iris. Did you also handle your business in the bushes?"
Ria yelped. "Also?! I didn't say that I did!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1373 Back At It Again
paragraphs: Ayame smirked at her. "Because you stopped before finishing the sentence." She turned slowly as her horrible grin deepened across her face and her eyes locked onto Iris. It was sharp. Deliberate. Infuratingly so. "So, dearest Iris. Explain the logistics of your waste management skills to me."
Iris's temperature dropped instantly. Her spine straightened. The air around her felt thinner. "I will kill you."
"Oh~" Ayame giggled softly, utterly unfazed. "Terrifying~"

Ria sputtered, trying to interject, when Iris snapped back, voice flat and venomous. "Shut your trap, you damned midget. Are we certain you're truly Miss Black Fang's and Kaede's sister? I wouldn't be shocked to learn that you're Thorga's long-lost sibling instead. You were probably also dropped on your head as a baby, by the way."
Then, just for good measure, the raven-haired, slightly unhinged woman with a foul mouth - at least when it came to interacting with the world's most annoying woman - spat, "You dumb slut."
The elves stationed along the hill, who were acutely listening in, making use of their station to glean some information about this truly strange group, froze.
A heartbeat passed.

Then several of them had to clamp their hands over their mouths. Shoulders shook. Eyes watered. Everyone knew who Thorga was; she was a known dwarven soldier who had a long and prestigious career in the army of Elvardia.
Ayame's grin vanished as if it never existed.
Her posture changed, subtle but absolute. Her hand drifted toward her blade.
"So you have chosen death."
Steel whispered as the duo stood and weapons began to move.
The sound followed Quinlan as he stepped through the portal.
Space closed behind him, cutting off laughter, curses, and the rising tension on the hill. He didn't look back. If the women took it too far, the others would intervene.
Hopefully.
The siege vanished. The noise fell away.
Only the three of them remained.
Blossom lifted her head, looking at him. "Master," she began with complete sincerity, "Blossom thinks Ayame and Iris are great friends!"
Quinlan's brow lifted. His mouth curved into something wry. "You think so?"
Liora stood a step behind them, hands folded at her waist. Her face stayed calm, almost flat, though her eyes lingered on Blossom for a moment longer than necessary. She said nothing.
"Yes!" Blossom nodded so hard her ears bounced. "Blossom can tell. Beneath all the thorns, there are two roses that love each other very much. Enough to die for each other!"
Quinlan paused.
Then he looked down at her. "Would you look at that. My sexy dogkin babe is becoming a poet. Who would've guessed?"
"Hehe!" Blossom puffed up proudly. "Blossom has been learning hard words with her mother, Natalie! Blossom doesn't want to look like a dumb pet."
Quinlan's hand slid up her back, steady and warm. "Hey. You were never anything like that. You're an amazing girl, even if your vocabulary isn't that of a poet."
Her smile softened.

She leaned in, pressing a gentle kiss to his cheek while her tail slowed, brushing against his leg. "Blossom loves Master," she decreed quietly. "But Blossom will try her best to become a wife who can proudly stand next to him. Now that Master is pursuing ladies like Black Fang... Blossom feels a little small."
Quinlan turned his head and kissed her in return. He rested his forehead against hers. "You have no reason to feel that way. But I can see you've already made up your mind."
His thumb brushed beneath her ear. "So instead of deterring you, I'll cheer you on."
Blossom didn't answer.
She just purred, long and deep, and curled closer in his arms.
"Inadequate," Liora suddenly spoke up.

"Hmm?" Quinlan and Blossom both asked in sync, turning toward the woman. The priestess smiled as she looked at Blossom and explained, "Miss Blossom, you said you felt small after comparing yourself to Lady Black Fang. I think using the word 'inadequate' instead of 'small' makes you seem a lot more like a prim and proper lady."
Blossom's ears twitched.
"Inadequ... what was it again?" she murmured to herself, lips moving as she rolled the word around. Her posture straightened little by little. Her eyes brightened. "Inadequate."
She nodded to herself, tail giving a pleased swish. "Yes!" She turned toward Liora and dipped her head politely. "Thank you for teaching Blossom a hard word."
Then she hesitated, glancing up again. "But please don't call Blossom 'Miss.' Blossom is just Blossom to her friends."
Liora's lips curved gently. "Is that so? You are welcome, Blossom."
The space between them felt easy after that. Quiet in a way that did not ask for silence. Quinlan was truly happy to witness this adorable interaction.
They stopped before a wooden door. Quinlan shifted Blossom in his arms and raised a hand.
Knock. Knock.
"Coming!" a female voice called from inside.
The door opened.

Kaelira stood there in loose pajamas patterned with tiny crossed hammers. The fabric hung comfortably, sleeves pushed up to her elbows. She thought the design looked tough; she loved the attire that was gifted to her by the team she led.

However, everyone else who had seen them agreed they were painfully cute. This was never mentioned aloud because the tomboy elf with a tantalizing six-pack would refuse to wear this piece of fabric if she ever found out, and literally no one wanted that to happen.
Her eyes went wide.
She stared at Quinlan as if he had stepped out of a forge fire.

"My lord, I didn't expect you... Aren't you fighting right now?" she whispered before stopping herself short when she realized the change in Quinlan's eyes. She understood that he wasn't happy with something, and she also understood what it was that displeased him.

Her shoulders drew in. Her hands clenched at her sides. She took a breath, then another, clearly wrestling with the words. "Quinlan," she corrected, the name stiff on her tongue. "My p-partner. Not just in the smithy b-but... life as well."
The faint color along her cheeks deepened as she looked anywhere but his eyes.

Quinlan's eyes, on the other hand, began to dance, once again happy. He positioned Blossom so she only occupied one arm and stepped closer, lifting a hand. His fingers slid into her lush, blue-tinged hair and began stroking it slowly, from crown to shoulder.
"Good girl," he purred.

sentences.text: Ayame smirked at her.
"Because you stopped before finishing the sentence." She turned slowly as her horrible grin deepened across her face and her eyes locked onto Iris.
It was sharp.
Deliberate.
Infuratingly so.
"So, dearest Iris.
Explain the logistics of your waste management skills to me."
Iris's temperature dropped instantly.
Her spine straightened.
The air around her felt thinner.
"I will kill you."
"Oh~" Ayame giggled softly, utterly unfazed.
"Terrifying~"
Ria sputtered, trying to interject, when Iris snapped back, voice flat and venomous.
"Shut your trap, you damned midget.
Are we certain you're truly Miss Black Fang's and Kaede's sister?
I wouldn't be shocked to learn that you're Thorga's long-lost sibling instead.
You were probably also dropped on your head as a baby, by the way."
Then, just for good measure, the raven-haired, slightly unhinged woman with a foul mouth - at least when it came to interacting with the world's most annoying woman - spat, "You dumb slut."
The elves stationed along the hill, who were acutely listening in, making use of their station to glean some information about this truly strange group, froze.
A heartbeat passed.
Then several of them had to clamp their hands over their mouths.
Shoulders shook.
Eyes watered.
Everyone knew who Thorga was; she was a known dwarven soldier who had a long and prestigious career in the army of Elvardia.
Ayame's grin vanished as if it never existed.
Her posture changed, subtle but absolute.
Her hand drifted toward her blade.
"So you have chosen death."
Steel whispered as the duo stood and weapons began to move.
The sound followed Quinlan as he stepped through the portal.
Space closed behind him, cutting off laughter, curses, and the rising tension on the hill.
He didn't look back.
If the women took it too far, the others would intervene.
Hopefully.
The siege vanished.
The noise fell away.
Only the three of them remained.
Blossom lifted her head, looking at him.
"Master," she began with complete sincerity, "Blossom thinks Ayame and Iris are great friends!"
Quinlan's brow lifted.
His mouth curved into something wry.
"You think so?"
Liora stood a step behind them, hands folded at her waist.
Her face stayed calm, almost flat, though her eyes lingered on Blossom for a moment longer than necessary.
She said nothing.
"Yes!" Blossom nodded so hard her ears bounced.
"Blossom can tell.
Beneath all the thorns, there are two roses that love each other very much.
Enough to die for each other!"
Quinlan paused.
Then he looked down at her.
"Would you look at that.
My sexy dogkin babe is becoming a poet.
Who would've guessed?"
"Hehe!" Blossom puffed up proudly.
"Blossom has been learning hard words with her mother, Natalie!
Blossom doesn't want to look like a dumb pet."
Quinlan's hand slid up her back, steady and warm.
"Hey.
You were never anything like that.
You're an amazing girl, even if your vocabulary isn't that of a poet."
Her smile softened.
She leaned in, pressing a gentle kiss to his cheek while her tail slowed, brushing against his leg.
"Blossom loves Master," she decreed quietly.
"But Blossom will try her best to become a wife who can proudly stand next to him.
Now that Master is pursuing ladies like Black Fang...
Blossom feels a little small."
Quinlan turned his head and kissed her in return.
He rested his forehead against hers.
"You have no reason to feel that way.
But I can see you've already made up your mind."
His thumb brushed beneath her ear.
"So instead of deterring you, I'll cheer you on."
Blossom didn't answer.
She just purred, long and deep, and curled closer in his arms.
"Inadequate," Liora suddenly spoke up.
"Hmm?" Quinlan and Blossom both asked in sync, turning toward the woman.
The priestess smiled as she looked at Blossom and explained, "Miss Blossom, you said you felt small after comparing yourself to Lady Black Fang.
I think using the word 'inadequate' instead of 'small' makes you seem a lot more like a prim and proper lady."
Blossom's ears twitched.
"Inadequ... what was it again?" she murmured to herself, lips moving as she rolled the word around.
Her posture straightened little by little.
Her eyes brightened.
"Inadequate."
She nodded to herself, tail giving a pleased swish.
"Yes!" She turned toward Liora and dipped her head politely.
"Thank you for teaching Blossom a hard word."
Then she hesitated, glancing up again.
"But please don't call Blossom 'Miss.' Blossom is just Blossom to her friends."
Liora's lips curved gently.
"Is that so?
You are welcome, Blossom."
The space between them felt easy after that.
Quiet in a way that did not ask for silence.
Quinlan was truly happy to witness this adorable interaction.
They stopped before a wooden door.
Quinlan shifted Blossom in his arms and raised a hand.
Knock.
Knock.
"Coming!" a female voice called from inside.
The door opened.
Kaelira stood there in loose pajamas patterned with tiny crossed hammers.
The fabric hung comfortably, sleeves pushed up to her elbows.
She thought the design looked tough; she loved the attire that was gifted to her by the team she led.
However, everyone else who had seen them agreed they were painfully cute.
This was never mentioned aloud because the tomboy elf with a tantalizing six-pack would refuse to wear this piece of fabric if she ever found out, and literally no one wanted that to happen.
Her eyes went wide.
She stared at Quinlan as if he had stepped out of a forge fire.
"My lord, I didn't expect you...
Aren't you fighting right now?" she whispered before stopping herself short when she realized the change in Quinlan's eyes.
She understood that he wasn't happy with something, and she also understood what it was that displeased him.
Her shoulders drew in.
Her hands clenched at her sides.
She took a breath, then another, clearly wrestling with the words.
"Quinlan," she corrected, the name stiff on her tongue.
"My p-partner.
Not just in the smithy b-but... life as well."
The faint color along her cheeks deepened as she looked anywhere but his eyes.
Quinlan's eyes, on the other hand, began to dance, once again happy.
He positioned Blossom so she only occupied one arm and stepped closer, lifting a hand.
His fingers slid into her lush, blue-tinged hair and began stroking it slowly, from crown to shoulder.
"Good girl," he purred.

chapters.title: Chapter 1374 Last Member
paragraphs: "Good girl," he purred.
Kaelira went red all at once. "Stop messing with me...!!" she muttered, turning her face away without much conviction.
"That is not messing with you!" Blossom chirped at once, tail wagging. "Master calling someone a good girl is big praise! Kaelira should be proud!"

Kaelira sent the dogkin a quick, helpless glance while the heat in her face only deepened. Clearly, being called a good girl by Quinlan had a 'slightly' different meaning to the two ladies. Then, the elf cleared her throat as she looked at her feet and began grumbling. "Why are you here to begin with? Was it just to tease me? So cruel..."
Quinlan's hand slid from her hair. His fingers moved under her chin, and he lifted her head gently until she had no choice but to meet his eyes.
Upon witnessing the beyond gorgeous sight that was his tomboy lover with red cheeks, he couldn't help but breathe, "... Beautiful."
"!!!" Her long ears flushed next.
"Messing with you?" Quinlan continued, tone light. "Me? I would never."
"Hmph," Kaelira scoffed, not believing that for a second.
He smiled anyway. "I have decided that I will hit level fifty today. I want you there with us when I do it."
The shift was instant.

"But..." she started. "Synchra's creation drained me greatly, and unlike you, I can't recover quickly... It's possible I'll never be able to create another Anima-rarity gear..." Her ears drooped at that as she added, "You said that until 'the doctor' says otherwise, I cannot fight."

"We'll look into your ability to recover from Anima creation later and evaluate..." Quinlan replied, gently stroking her chin. He knew how heavily the knowledge weighed on the elf because her body almost gave out; she likely won't be able to create another piece of work like Synchra. After all, merely getting higher Vitality wouldn't solve the problem, as it drained both her body and soul. Quinlan helped her recover, but who knew how she would react if she was drained like that again?
There's a good chance she'd perish on the spot.
Quinlan grinned and changed the topic before her ears could droop any further. "And, as for 'the doctor...'"
Liora leaned out from behind his broad frame and gave a wave to her captain with a grin. "Hello."
Kaelira's eyes narrowed to slits as she looked at the woman who had personally ordered her to stay behind while the others fought. "It's you..." she murmured.
"Yes. It is I, Captain," Liora replied cheerfully. Then added, "Please stop glaring at me like that in your epic gear, or I might just pee myself a little."
Without waiting for a response or an invitation, she stepped into the room and took Kaelira by the wrist, tugging her inside.

Quinlan followed and, together with the girl who refused to leave his arms, settled near the bed in a comfortable chair. Blossom claimed his lap at once, curling into him with a satisfied hum. Both of them watched as Liora went to work.
"Lie down," Liora said, already rolling up one sleeve.
Kaelira hesitated, then did as told, sitting back and easing onto the bed. She stared at the ceiling with her hands folded over her stomach.
"[Sanctified Pulse]," Liora intoned.
Light bloomed at her fingertip. It burned clean and steady, like a focused ember.
"Do not move," Liora added, then pressed her finger lightly against Kaelira's collarbone.

The priestess traced downward in slow lines. Shoulder. Sternum. Along the curve of her ribs. The light followed, sinking through fabric and skin alike, slipping past cloth without disturbing it. The spell did not need access directly to her skin; it read what lay beneath.
Kaelira's breathing changed as the finger continued, passing over her abdomen, then lower, then back up again, mapping her frame with careful precision. Muscles tightened. Relaxed. Tightened again.
Blossom leaned closer, chin resting against Quinlan's chest, eyes wide with interest. Quinlan stayed still with one hand resting on Blossom's thighs and another on her head.
Seconds stretched until Liora finally pulled her hand away. The light faded.
She smiled. "You are almost fully recovered. Your body is stable."
Kaelira sat up at once. "So I can go?"
"... Yes. But you must be careful, is that understood?" The priestess looked very sternly at the elf. "Do not push yourself. If you feel strain, tell us, and we will withdraw."
"Yes," Kaelira replied, already swinging her legs off the bed.

She bounced to her feet, grin breaking free, and rushed toward her armor stand. In her hurry, she peeled off the pajama top and trousers without a second thought, already reaching for steel and leather while buck naked.
Blossom reacted instantly.
She stretched up and clapped both hands over Quinlan's eyes. "Master, no peeking... Kaelira is not ready. She would have a heart attack."
Quinlan let out a small, pained sound but did not resist. His hands stayed where they were. "What a cruel fate I must endure..." he whined.
Blossom leaned close and kissed him. "Is it still a cruel fate, Master?"
"I am the most blessed man in the universe."
"Hehe!"
Ahead of them, Kaelira turned around, ready with her armor on, and yelped. The sound came out sharp and panicked as her face flared hot all at once.
She had forgotten he was there.
Her gaze flicked to Quinlan's covered eyes. Then to Blossom, who was smiling at her with obvious pride.
"... Thank you," Kaelira muttered, realizing what was going on. "I'm such a ditz! I can't believe it..."
Blossom's tail wagged harder.
Kaelira grabbed her hammer. She rolled her shoulders once, then looked to Quinlan.
"I am ready."
Quinlan nodded and stood. "Then let us go."
He raised his hand again. "[Warp Gate]."
Space folded.
They stepped through.
On the far side, the air shook.

The barrier below shattered at that exact moment they arrived, light collapsing inward as the final runes failed. The dome vanished. Smoke rolled forward. The siege line roared in victory. "Give them steel, lads!" the shouts began. It was time.

chapters.title: Chapter 1375 Time to Resume
paragraphs: The elves stationed along the hill gasped as one as they witnessed the sight of every woman rising from her seat at the same instant. As soon as the barrier protecting the city came off, laughter cut off mid-breath. Smirks vanished. Postures straightened, spines aligning as if drawn by a single thread.
Then space folded.

A dark seam opened in the air a dozen steps ahead of them, edges curling inward. The man stepped through first. The blonde dogkin followed, pressed close at his side. The elves recognized the pair at once.
Then came the third.
A figure clad head to toe in heavy armor stepped through the gate. Broad pauldrons. Reinforced greaves. A warhammer held at her side. The metal was practical, built to endure rather than impress.
The elves' ears twitched.
Something tugged at their senses. A trace of familiarity that refused to settle. The presence carried a faint resonance they had felt since childhood.
Elf.
But no elf they knew wore armor like that.

No elven warrior would wear such an ugly, masculine thing. It was too cumbersome. Too enclosed. Too far removed from the living world. Heavy armor severed one's connection to Mother Nature, and elves did not tolerate that kind of separation. From the moment they could walk, they were taught to feel the ground beneath their feet. Bare soles against soil, stone, grass. That contact was not traditional for tradition's sake. It was communication. The land whispered warnings, lent balance, guided movement. To encase one's body in layers of dead metal was to willingly go deaf.
Elves were never clumsy creatures. Not even the scholars.

While not every elf was a ranger, every elf was a lithe fighter. Mage, assassin, archer, duelist, even those who claimed to be pure fighters still moved with a grace born from centuries of instinct. Their garbs were light, flexible, cut to flow rather than resist. Fabric and leather that bent with motion. Armor that protected without obstructing. Speed and precision were their creed. Agility was survival.
That woman violated all of it.

Her armor was thick. Reinforced. Built to absorb impact rather than avoid it. Every plate locked into place with brutal purpose. Nothing about it yielded. Nothing invited motion. It was the kind of equipment meant for the clumsy denizens of Iksaris, also known as humans and dwarves, who relied on endurance and brute strength rather than finesse.
So the elves dismissed the thought.
She had to be human.

Why not a halfling? 'Halfling,' the child born from the union of two races, was not exactly a thing on the continent of Iskaris. Tries have been made, of course, but they have not led anywhere. Some scholars argued that it was because these trials took place between a master and a slave, who tended to be unwilling and stressed.
It was observed that animals didn't breed well while in a stressful environment, so they reasoned, why would it be different for humanoids?

But that logic was brought into question by saying that not only should it happen at least rarely, even if the female was under duress, but also, throughout history, there were loving relationships between members of different races.

The Alliance of Elvardia came to be because the elf queen of old fell in love with the dwarf king, and the two decided to join their people in creating the empire they have now. Both of them being on the brink of destruction due to the Vraven Kingdom and the Beastman Confederation certainly helped make the unlikely alliance happen.
However, despite their loving relationship, the elf queen never conceived a child from her husband, and similar outcomes were recorded the few times romance occurred between members of the two races.

This was the main reason why elven women, cursed with having elven men who can't level up and thus die much earlier than their female counterparts, tended to either live life without a partner or find solace in the company of other elven women.

Since they couldn't conceive children from unions with men of other races, who would die sooner than they anyhow, they decided it was for the best to treat their elven men as studs when they felt ready to have kids, but only have romantic relationships with other elven women.
This all explained why the armored woman could not be an elf. No one would ever choose to limit themselves like this.

So the elves turned their full attention back to Quinlan, unaware of how wrong they were. Being a tanker didn't limit Kaelira. In fact, thanks to her new class, which evolved after inhaling Rosie's flower, Kaelira's dream of being the best smith while also protecting her loved ones could be achieved all at once.
After all, being the Runeweaver Titan, she could do both at once.

They shook the thought off and refocused on the tall and ominous man. His mere presence made the elves feel uneasy, especially after learning of who he was and how he thought Elvardia had to prove itself worthy of his alliance, not the other way around.
They found him greatly arrogant, but just as unnerving as well, making them act reserved.

Quinlan stood at the edge of the hill, armor sealed and silent. The wind tugged at his cloak as he looked over his allies. He did not address the women, nor did he give orders. Instead, he merely looked back once, with the red orbs that were his eyes passing over them with ominous intent.
Then he raised one hand.
No chant followed.
No flourish.
The air changed.

A pressure settled over the hill, subtle at first, then unmistakable. Grass bent outward in a slow ripple. Dust lifted from the soil, circling his boots in widening arcs. The elves stiffened as their instincts screamed at them that whatever this being truly was, his relationship with Mother Nature and the four elements was vastly different than what their kind knew.
The breeze deepened. Thickened. It wrapped around the women like unseen arms.
Together, their feet left the ground. Bodies rose in perfect sync, and then the wind surged.

They shot forward as one, silently shooting above the battlefield and streaked toward the city where the barrier had fallen. Smoke rolled up to meet them. Firelight reflected off steel and skin alike. Then they were gone, swallowed by distance and haze.
Only then did the hill breathe again.
Several elves sagged where they stood. One braced both hands against her bow, exhaling slowly. Another rubbed at their chest as if easing a tight knot.
"... I couldn't move," one muttered.
"I've stood before ancient treants," another said quietly. "This was worse."
A third swallowed. "It felt like the sky was watching us."
Their ears flicked, greatly unsettled. "Lady Luminara protect us..." a fourth whispered.
Then one of them frowned. "Wait. That woman. The one with the purple sheen in her eyes."
A pause came as she nearly cried, "Wasn't that the notorious Black Fang?!"
Murmurs spread at once.
"The criminal?"
"One of the three strongest human women alive?"
"Can that be?"
"The pink-haired woman that was next to her! I heard her second-in-command is a short, curvaceous, floral-tattooed, pink-haired human woman!"
"Orianna is the name," one nodded grimly. "I also saw two who fit the two other members of her lieutenant squad, Raika and Vex."
"Why are they following him... Why is that young upstart with her terrifying class not calling the shots?" someone whispered.

To these elves, Black Fang was but a new kid on the block, showcasing the difference between the two races and their perception of time. Black Fang was worried about growing wrinkles, while to the elves, she was a newcomer. Barely an adult.

Another shook their head slowly. "Not just following. She moved when he moved. I'm not sure what's going on between them, but I'm confident she trusts him greatly, just like the rest of his companions do."
Silence fell again.
"That man..." an elf said at last, voice low. "He's terrifying."
No one argued.
"D-do you think he's doing... all of them?"
The question slipped out before the young elf could stop it.

She stood at the back of the sentry line, hands clasped together before her chest, ears tipped forward despite herself. Compared to the others, she was still new to the watch. Her armor fit a little too cleanly. Her bowstring had not yet frayed from years of use.
The older elves turned toward her in unison.
Dry looks met her wide eyes.
"Eilwen..." one of them said flatly, "do not get ideas."
Another snorted. "That path leads to disappointment and a lot of unnecessary drama."
Eilwen's face lit up in a furious shade of red. "I am not getting ideas!" she snapped, stamping a foot. "I'm just asking. So answer me, you old hags!"

Since they couldn't conceive children from unions with men of other races, who would die sooner than they anyhow, they decided it was for the best to treat their elven men as studs when they felt ready to have kids, but only have romantic relationships with other elven women.
This all explained why the armored woman could not be an elf.
No one would ever choose to limit themselves like this.
So the elves turned their full attention back to Quinlan, unaware of how wrong they were.
Being a tanker didn't limit Kaelira.
In fact, thanks to her new class, which evolved after inhaling Rosie's flower, Kaelira's dream of being the best smith while also protecting her loved ones could be achieved all at once.
After all, being the Runeweaver Titan, she could do both at once.
They shook the thought off and refocused on the tall and ominous man.
His mere presence made the elves feel uneasy, especially after learning of who he was and how he thought Elvardia had to prove itself worthy of his alliance, not the other way around.
They found him greatly arrogant, but just as unnerving as well, making them act reserved.
Quinlan stood at the edge of the hill, armor sealed and silent.
The wind tugged at his cloak as he looked over his allies.
He did not address the women, nor did he give orders.
Instead, he merely looked back once, with the red orbs that were his eyes passing over them with ominous intent.
Then he raised one hand.
No chant followed.
No flourish.
The air changed.
A pressure settled over the hill, subtle at first, then unmistakable.
Grass bent outward in a slow ripple.
Dust lifted from the soil, circling his boots in widening arcs.
The elves stiffened as their instincts screamed at them that whatever this being truly was, his relationship with Mother Nature and the four elements was vastly different than what their kind knew.
The breeze deepened.
Thickened.
It wrapped around the women like unseen arms.
Together, their feet left the ground.
Bodies rose in perfect sync, and then the wind surged.
They shot forward as one, silently shooting above the battlefield and streaked toward the city where the barrier had fallen.
Smoke rolled up to meet them.
Firelight reflected off steel and skin alike.
Then they were gone, swallowed by distance and haze.
Only then did the hill breathe again.
Several elves sagged where they stood.
One braced both hands against her bow, exhaling slowly.
Another rubbed at their chest as if easing a tight knot.
I couldn't move," one muttered.
"I've stood before ancient treants," another said quietly.
"This was worse."
A third swallowed.
"It felt like the sky was watching us."
Their ears flicked, greatly unsettled.
"Lady Luminara protect us..." a fourth whispered.
Then one of them frowned.
"Wait.
That woman.
The one with the purple sheen in her eyes."
A pause came as she nearly cried, "Wasn't that the notorious Black Fang?!"
Murmurs spread at once.
"The criminal?"
"One of the three strongest human women alive?"
"Can that be?"
"The pink-haired woman that was next to her!
I heard her second-in-command is a short, curvaceous, floral-tattooed, pink-haired human woman!"
"Orianna is the name," one nodded grimly.
"I also saw two who fit the two other members of her lieutenant squad, Raika and Vex."
"Why are they following him...
Why is that young upstart with her terrifying class not calling the shots?" someone whispered.
To these elves, Black Fang was but a new kid on the block, showcasing the difference between the two races and their perception of time.
Black Fang was worried about growing wrinkles, while to the elves, she was a newcomer.
Barely an adult.
Another shook their head slowly.
"Not just following.
She moved when he moved.
I'm not sure what's going on between them, but I'm confident she trusts him greatly, just like the rest of his companions do."
Silence fell again.
"That man..." an elf said at last, voice low.
"He's terrifying."
No one argued.
"D-do you think he's doing... all of them?"
The question slipped out before the young elf could stop it.
She stood at the back of the sentry line, hands clasped together before her chest, ears tipped forward despite herself.
Compared to the others, she was still new to the watch.
Her armor fit a little too cleanly.
Her bowstring had not yet frayed from years of use.
The older elves turned toward her in unison.
Dry looks met her wide eyes.
"Eilwen..." one of them said flatly, "do not get ideas."
Another snorted.
"That path leads to disappointment and a lot of unnecessary drama."
Eilwen's face lit up in a furious shade of red.
"I am not getting ideas!" she snapped, stamping a foot.
"I'm just asking.
So answer me, you old hags!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1376 Tragic Fate of Elven Girls
paragraphs: "I'm just asking. So answer me, you old hags!"
Several brows twitched.
"Watch your mouth, damned brat..." one muttered.
A brief silence followed. Then an archer who had been watching quietly spoke, voice measured. "No. They are not all his lovers."
Eilwen leaned forward. "How do you know?"

"I saw two children among them," the elf replied. "And many of the women looked at him the way one looks at a commander. Respect, trust, and expectation. Those were not the eyes of women looking at their lover."
Eilwen deflated slightly. "Oh."

Another elf tilted her head, lips curling up into a giant grin. "Though," she added, "he is clearly a busy man. I counted at least two handfuls of women who looked at him like he was their whole world."
Eilwen's head snapped up. "Ten?!" she yelped, hands flying to her cheeks while her thighs rubbed together. "He must be very talented..."
She stared out toward the distant city where Quinlan had flown off toward with eyes that were unfocused, clearly picturing something that had nothing to do with tactics or alliances.
"Haaah..." she sighed wistfully.

One of the older sentries clicked her tongue. "That settles it. It's time for you to find a nice girl and tie the knot. You're a lonely woman, Eilwen. You need a good partner before your head drifts any further into the clouds."
Another nodded. "A steady hand. Someone warm. Someone who knows how to stay."

Eilwen snapped around, scandalized. "Hah?!" she barked. "I'm not into that gay nonsense, you zesty old hags. I want a big, strong, handsome man to take care of me. Not a woman licking me while shoving a finger up there."
Her expression turned to that of sheer disgust. "Ew. Ewww...." Then she began making gagging sounds.
The hill went very still.
Several pairs of eyes narrowed.
"Excuse us?" one of them asked slowly. As a lesbian with thousands of years of cunnilingus experience, she was incredibly offended right now.
"Watch your tongue, brat," another hissed. "A loving female companion is the way Lady Luminara intended for our kind to live. You would do well to remember that."

Eilwen rolled her eyes and let out a long sigh. "Oh, please. Who are you to put words in the first elf's mouth? Did you hear Lady Luminara say such a thing herself? Do you have a writing that came directly from her hands?" She waved a hand toward the smoke-choked city in the distance. "And if that really was the elven way, then explain something to me. Why did that blonde elf with big tits and thick thighs next to him look happier than any elf I've ever seen? She was not calm. Not 'at peace with what life gave her.' She was simply happy. Like she actually mattered. Like she belonged. Like she had an actual lover she was attracted to wholeheartedly, instead of settling for a lesbian because that was the best course of action to not be lonely."
The older woman fell quiet.
They exchanged looks. Long ones. The kind that carried too many thoughts and not enough answers.
No one spoke.

Eilwen turned back toward the horizon with her arms folded and ears twitching. "Yeah," she muttered. Then her eyes narrowed. "That's what I thought. So the next time I crave a hot guy's embrace, no one preaches to me about the joy of licking puss, is that understood? Damned old hags."
A long breath passed through the line.
Then another.
Then leather creaked.
Eilwen's ears flicked.
Slowly, very slowly, she turned her head.

Three of the older sentries were already stepping forward. Calm. Deliberate. Expressions carved from stone. One had unbuckled her belt. Another was halfway through doing the same. The third rolled the leather free with a soft, practiced tug.
The sound snapped something into place in Eilwen's mind.
The word came out small.
One of the women spoke at a voice level. "You are a disgrace to elven kind."
Another nodded. "You speak like a common dwarven whore shouting from a tavern table."
The third tested the belt in her hands, folding it once. "And since your mouth clearly does not understand restraint, we will teach it. We will teach you how to become a proper elven lady, Eilwen."
"We do it because we love you."
"Always remember that."
Eilwen's spine went rigid.
"H-Hey now," she said quickly, laughter pitching too high. "Let's all take a breath. No need to escalate. Words were exchanged. Cultural differences. Generational misunderstandings."
They kept walking.
Her eyes darted left. Right. The hill behind her offered nothing but open ground and witnesses who suddenly found the sky very interesting.
"I was joking," she tried. "You know. Humor. It's a thing now. Among younger elves. We say outrageous things for bonding and to help us endure our cruel fate of leading a long, loveless life."
One of the belts slid fully free.
"That explains nothing," came the reply.
"We don't care if you tie the knot with an elven woman or not, Eilwen. Many elves are happy leading a single life. It was just a suggestion we made when we saw how lonely you were."
"But what we do care about is your terrible lack of respect for your elders."
"Poor girl's mother died soon after her birth... I realize that we, members of the old guard, failed to take care of the child of one of our own."
"We'll rectify that right now."
Eilwen took a step back.
Then another.
"Wait," she yelped, palms up. "Wait, wait, wait. I think I may have overextended my commentary. Just a little. Maybe more than a little."
She laughed again, this time with visible panic. "In my defense, I forgot I was stationed with traditional grannies instead of people my age."
The women stopped in front of her.
They loomed.
Eilwen swallowed.
"... I ran my mouth too long, didn't I?"
One of them smiled. It was not kind.
"Bend over," she ordered.
Eilwen yelped and spun, sprinting three steps before a hand caught her long, flowing hair and hauled her to a stop.
"No running," another added. "That just adds rounds."

"I retract everything!" Eilwen cried. "All statements. Entire philosophy. I respect tradition. Lady Luminara herself could not be more disappointed in me than I already am. I love women. Licking puss is my life's greatest mission! Penises are so ugly and disgusting, ew!"

Her cheeks began to brighten as she got into it, eyes turning dreamy. "Imagine the nightmare of having a broad-shouldered, muscular, chiseled, handsome man tower over you as he takes you in bed, and kisses you while his weight presses down, warm skin against mine, and heavy breathing in my ears as he pushes me into the mattress with his weight alone. He then whispers encouraging words to me as he enters my eagerly awaiting hole like a true, loving gentleman... "
The belt snapped once through the air.
Eilwen squeaked.

"Ah, I got carried away again! By the leaves, I'm sorry! I will never speak of anything again. I will meditate. I will take vows. My dream is to become a raging lesbian with a harem of horny elven sluts!"
The belts came down.
The hill echoed with a yelp that carried halfway to the city. Several elves winced.
None intervened.
Motherly justice, elven style, was being administered.
An older sentry watching from the side shook her head. "This is why we keep the youth supervised."
Another sighed. "A mouth like that was bound to catch consequences."
"They even explained to her that they're not mad because she refuses to embrace another woman... Many of us refuse that... Eilwen simply can't shut her trap to save the life of her."
"True.."
The onlookers were in complete agreement.
As the cries of the younger elf were swallowed by the hill and the grannies set about their work, Quinlan reached his destination.
The wind steadied beneath him.

He hovered high above the city, cloak drawn back, boots held aloft by invisible currents. Below, Elvardian forces were pushing to take the walls in disciplined waves. Inside the walls, the dead were already loose.

Undead shapes flooded alleys and plazas, breaking lines, dragging defenders down, forcing chaos where structure had once stood. Smoke climbed in uneven columns. Fires spread without pattern. The city fought on two fronts and did not yet understand it.
Quinlan's gaze moved slowly, taking it in. The timing. The pressure. The way fear and momentum tangled together.
A grin cut across his face.
"What a beautiful sight."
