His gaze swept across the garden again.
"Rosie is going to love this place."
Luminara's reaction was immediate.
Her grip tightened and her steps picked up, the rhythm of her skipping turning quicker.
"I cannot wait to meet her!
I upgraded my home as well in hopes of impressing her.
This is just a road."
"This is just a road...?" Quinlan repeated while listening to the literal chorus of the animated flowers.
It seemed that Luminara had entered pampering grandmother mode months prior.
He let himself be pulled along again.
After a moment, he looked down at the stone beneath his feet.
"So is this road the gift you mentioned?"
Miri and Luminara exchanged a glance, then laughed together.
"One of many," Miri replied.
"Did you truly think we would prepare only one present?" Luminara added, her voice bright.
"We had months."
Miri nodded firmly.
"This is only the warm-up!"
"Is that so..." They continued on at an easy pace.
Minutes passed with no one rushing ahead.
All three of them felt the desire to cherish this moment.
Quinlan let his shoulders relax.
There was no urgency here.
No trial timer.
No pressure to perform.
Just movement, shared and familiar.
He could stay for weeks now.
At first, he had to leave after a couple of days due to the lingering divinity in the air.
However, these days, as he leveled up, his resistances grew stronger, letting him stay for longer periods.
After a while, he spoke again.
"Earlier," he said, glancing toward Luminara, "you mentioned I would be able to enter this place on my own one day.
How does that work?
When exactly?"
The skipping slowed.
Miri and Luminara exchanged a brief look.
"We cannot answer questions like that, Quinnie...
I'm sorry..." Luminara apologized with ears that drooped dejectedly.
Miri nodded in agreement, but added, "You should focus on reaching level one hundred first."
Quinlan dipped his head.
"Understood.
I am sorry."
His thoughts had already gone elsewhere, to a quiet conversation long ago.
Malakar, the old human primordial's warning, returned to him in full clarity.
There were questions tied to bindings and old rules, questions his mothers were not allowed to answer.

Malakar had spoken out of concern for the pair of turbo mommies and their care for Quinlan that ran deep enough that they might have strained against restrictions meant to hold even primordials in place.
"There is nothing to apologize for, Quinnie!" they chirped together.
Both women leaned in at once, their heads resting against his shoulders from either side, steps resuming.
Their grip stayed firm and extremely affectionate.
Before long, the garden gave way to open ground.
Stone paths branched outward, leading toward scattered structures across the floating island.
Houses stood at varying distances from one another, some carved directly into rock, others built upward with layered platforms and open terraces.
Many showed signs of long disuse.
Quinlan took it in as they slowed near the edge of the settlement.
"I've been meaning to ask, but never got to it before.
Why were these abodes built?"
Miri answered this time.
"When the primordial dimension was used for its intended purpose, we only stayed here briefly."
Luminara nodded.
"Training.
Rest.
Preparation."
"Björn created this village so we could sleep and recover between joint training sessions," Miri continued.
"It was practical and efficient."
Her gaze drifted across the quiet homes.
"But that was a long time ago."
Luminara's lips curved slightly.
"Now we prefer privacy.
We have left the village, each of us creating a little pocket of home where we could bear with the cruel passage of time in a little more peace."
I see," Quinlan didn't know how to respond.
The primordials of Thalorind have been put through an extreme test of willpower.
He couldn't even begin to understand how he would deal with having been stuck here for millions of years.
With their potential mortal partners in the outside world growing old and dying...
He would've gone mad.

But these people, while some indeed seemed to have become unhinged - his mind moved to Nyxara, whose first thought was to rape him as soon as she smelled 'a newborn primordial' - many of them displayed extreme mental fortitude.
His mothers included.
"I'm proud of you two.
You're not just powerful, but incredibly resilient as well," he decreed.
"Quinnie..." the mothers smiled fondly together.
"We were rapidly losing our minds, truth be told... but then, the greatest gift of our life appeared on the doorstep...
You saved us."
Quinlan returned their tender smiles and his arms around the slim waists of his mothers strengthened.
And just like this, they arrived at the center of the village, where a surprise awaited Quinlan.

chapters.title: Chapter 1392 Surprise!
paragraphs: At the heart of the village, the paths converged into a broad clearing, where the tall monument needed to begin his trial could be seen.
An old man stood near the center with his hands tucked into the sleeves of a worn robe, posture bent. His beard was long and gray, and rather unkept. He looked up as the trio approached.
His expression soured immediately.
He squinted at Quinlan. Then, at Miri and Luminara clinging to him. Then back at Quinlan.
"...Laddy," he muttered, rubbing his temple with two fingers. "Aren't you a bit quick to return? Why not wait a couple of hundred years between each trial?"

The warmth on Quinlan's face vanished, replaced by a sharp grin that pulled at his lips, familiar and dangerous in a way that had nothing to do with hostility and everything to do with recognition. "Malakar, you grumpy old bastard. It's good to see you too."

The contrast struck him immediately. His mothers had called his return painfully slow, demanding justification. Even though he needed an immense amount of XP... Quinlan knew that he wasn't really slow. Rather, he was likely fast even for primordial standards due to the high-tier massacres he committed one after the other in the last few days.
Thus, it was more so that his mothers were missing him greatly. However... This old bastard thought it was rushed. By hundreds of years.
The reaction beside him was instant.
"A couple hundred years?!" Luminara hissed, ears snapping upright.
Miri spun on Malakar with narrowed eyes. "Have you gone senile?!"
"I'll beat you up!" Luminara added, already stepping forward.
"Stop spouting nonsense!" Miri snapped, tugging Quinlan half a step behind her like a shield in reverse.
The barrage continued without pause.
Malakar's grimace deepened by the second.

He raised both hands to his ears, then dropped them again when that failed to slow anything. His shoulders sagged. The lines on his face pulled tight as if he were enduring a migraine forged by the universe itself.
"I knew this would happen," he muttered under his breath. Then looked at Quinlan from the side of his eyes. "Go ahead, Laddy, begin your trial so you can leave quickly."
"Malakar!!" Miri growled, summoning her spear.
"You know our plan and agreed to it, so stop whining!" Luminara demanded.
The two mothers were entering extreme mama bear mode.
Miri jabbed a finger at him. "I'll teach you proper manners!"
Luminara narrowed her pupils. "Apologize."
Malakar closed his eyes. Opened them again. Pinched the bridge of his nose.
"This," he said slowly, voice flat with resignation, "is exactly why I warned you, Laddy. Women are crazy creatures. Yet you can't seem to get enough of them."
Quinlan's grin widened instead of fading, clearly enjoying himself. "How could I possibly get enough of them? Women are amazing. I love women."
The effect was immediate.

Luminara's ears relaxed, then tilted forward with visible satisfaction. Her posture softened, shoulders easing as she turned toward him with a pleased hum. Miri's scowl evaporated just as quickly, replaced by a warm look that carried far too much pride for a mother who had known him for months rather than eons.
Malakar watched the shift with a tired stare. He let out a long breath. "This mindset of yours will bring you nothing but headaches in the future."
Quinlan shrugged, entirely unbothered. "Perhaps the issue lies in how the two of us are treated by women. Have you considered that?"
Malakar's brow lifted a fraction.

Quinlan continued calmly. "Some of them try to beat me up. A few even want to dissect me or run experiments. That happens. But most are kind. They look out for me. They enjoy my company." He tilted his head, eyes flicking to Malakar's robe and then his beard. "You, on the other hand, present yourself as a grumpy old man who cannot even be bothered to keep his own appearance in order. It makes sense that women respond to us differently."
The air shifted.

Malakar's eyes narrowed, lines on his face tightening. His shoulders straightened just a little, age giving way to something older and sharper beneath the surface. "Laddy," he began quietly, "you always had a far too big mouth on you for your meager powers, but it seems it grows worse every time you return. Perhaps next time, it will be me waiting for you at the edge, rather than your mothers. I'll teach you some much-needed humility."
"That will never happen!" Miri and Luminara snapped together.
Luminara stepped forward, one hand planted on her hip, ears angled back in irritation. "And you were an infamous 'player' back in the day. Do not pretend otherwise."
Miri nodded sharply. "I heard that you chased anything that moved. Especially if they were frilly skirts."
Mearie was much younger than Malakar and Luminara; thus, she wasn't there back when the two were in their wild youths.
"You sired millions of children," Luminara added without hesitation. "So do not preach nonsense to our son."
Miri then added, "You know perfectly well that creating a large harem of healthy women is in his nature as a young male primordial. To start his lineage strong, he needs lots of healthy babies!"
"In fact, I'd say that our Quinnie is beyond conservative! He doesn't even have ten lovers, as opposed to you, who couldn't even remember the names of the women you lay with!" Lumi stomped.
"Uh... Mothers..."
"Yes, Quinnie?"
"The number is more than ten now..." Quinlan said, scratching the back of his neck.
"Oh, right!! We have new ladies to meet, evaluate, and judge!" The two of them perked up instantly.
Then sent Malakar a dismissive scoff. "So stop whining and get ready. We made a deal!"
"Yes, yes..." Malakar let out a long, put-upon sigh. Then, his hand slipped free from his sleeve.
A staff formed in his grasp without ceremony. Dark wood, worn smooth by age, its surface etched with shallow marks. The tip met the ground. "Come out, everyone. The brat is here," Malakar called.
The clearing answered.

A low surge rolled outward from the point of contact, magical pressure rather than sound. The air bent, space folding inward for a brief moment before settling again. The monument behind him remained unchanged, but the paths feeding into the clearing began to stir.
Figures stepped out one after another.
Some emerged from between buildings, others from open air where no doorway had been a heartbeat earlier.
Some of them he'd met before, many he hadn't.
"What is going on?" he asked, turning his head toward Miri and Luminara.
Luminara's face was bright, ears lifted high. Miri clasped her hands together, barely containing herself.
"This is our main present, Quinnie!"

"We went through the dimension and woke up the primordials we are on good terms with. We thought it was time for you to finally interact with them on a deeper level. They deserve to welcome the new primordial, and you deserve to glean some wisdom and experience from them!"
"And so that you and your lovers can learn from them," Miri continued. "No mortal alive today has such a privilege!"

Quinlan's gaze swept the gathering again. Several of the primordials were already looking at him, assessing without pretense. Others exchanged glances with his mothers, faint smiles passing between old acquaintances.
"They are also needed to help us envelop your girls in protective magic," Luminara added, tone firm now. "Malakar managed it for Serika and Feng last time, but..."
Malakar snorted, resting both hands on his staff. "I am not sustaining layered protection for dozens of people for weeks. No amount of payment will make me do that."
Miri nodded emphatically. "With this many of us, the burden can be shared."
"What do you two pay this grumpy grandpa in?" Quinlan asked gingerly.
"Silence..." Malakar grumbled. "They finally cease their endless chatter near me. For a while, that is."
"..." Quinlan's look turned slightly empathetic.
Luminara, not caring for the misery of Malakar, spread her arms wide, presenting the scene like a host unveiling a feast. "So this is our gift."
Miri beamed. "A primordial party!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1393 Meeting the Primordials
paragraphs: Quinlan took a slow breath and let his awareness spread. As he did so, he started recognizing faces.
Karl was the first to move closer.

The shapeshifter wore an immaculate black tuxedo, posture straight, shoes polished to a mirror shine. The contrast came from the head perched atop that refined body. A pig's face, pink snout twitching, small eyes sharp with intelligence. He adjusted his cufflinks, then bowed with perfect etiquette.
"Welcome back, son," Karl said smoothly while tipping his fedora.
He punctuated the greeting with a polite nod and an unmistakable oink.
Quinlan smiled. "Still refusing to pick a consistent form, I see."
Karl's tail flicked once behind him. "Consistency is for creatures who fear change."
Then he oinked a second time, averting Miri's and Lumi's gazes, "I only fear women. They are horrible, nasty creatures."
"Khm."

The two women holding Quinlan's hands gently coughed. Despite the delicate nature of their sound, Karl trembled and tipped his fedora a second time before stepping back behind Malakar, using the old man as a shield.
Quinlan chuckled amusedly before his attention shifted again.

A broad figure pushed through the gathering, each step heavy and grounded. The dwarf's presence felt like stone given breath. Thick arms crossed over a chest wrapped in layered leather and metal, beard braided tight with small runic clasps woven through.
"Björn," Quinlan greeted.

The primordial blacksmith grunted in response. "I hope you didn't shame my creation since I last saw you," he decreed. Indeed, the Soul Reaper was the creation of the Primordial Smith. Björn kept walking after Quinlan nodded. The dwarf was not alone.
Another dwarf walked beside him. Just as wide. Just as solid. The beard was longer, braided differently, and for a brief moment, Quinlan's mind stumbled.
Why is there another male dwarf primordial?
Primordials came in pairs.
There was only one dwarven primordial pair.
Then it clicked.
Quinlan forced a careful breath through his nose as understanding settled. The second dwarf was a woman.
Björn gestured to her. "This is my-"
He stopped.
Both dwarves leaned forward.
Their eyes narrowed in unison.
Their attention locked onto Quinlan's chest.
The red flames of Synchra rolled once beneath the armor's surface.
The two immediately began exchanging hushed notes between one another, whispering with a crafter's curiosity glinting in their eyes.
Quinlan wanted to speak more with the pair, but he never got the chance.
Heavy footsteps announced themselves from the far side of the clearing.

A woman emerged dressed in layered hides and thick cloth, colors echoing cold seas and stone cliffs. Her attire carried the shape of a barbarian's garb, practical and worn, yet it fit her aesthetic. Thick muscles lined her arms and shoulders without hiding her form. Her hair was dark and tied back.
Despite her rough, more masculine appearance, she was still a good-looking woman, just needing... An acquired taste to truly appreciate her beauty.
She stopped a short distance away.
Quinlan blinked once.
"Would you happen to be Thyra?" he asked and respectfully introduced himself. "Greetings, my name is Quinlan, the newest primordial and the son of Luminara and Mearie."

He remembered the stories. Malakar and Thyra. The first human pair. The foundation that was laid long before kingdoms learned to name themselves. Despite it being Mearie who stayed on the Iskaris Continent, Thyra had come far earlier.
The woman standing before him was the true mother of humanity. Almost all denizens of Iskaris descended from her and Malakar.
Thyra studied him for several heartbeats.
Then she stepped closer.
Only when she stood directly in front of him did Quinlan realize the full measure of it.
She was tall, extremely so.

Two meters (6'6") tall, to be exact, which meant she was standing eye to eye with Quinlan. She was the first woman who matched his height since his transformation with the Primordial Breeding Physique he unlocked before boning Blossom right after saving her from her slave contract.
Miri stepped forward before Quinlan could shift his weight.

She planted herself between them, shoulders squared, chin lifted as she looked up at the towering woman in front of her. Her fingers tightened around her spear, not raised, but ready. Her stance carried no hesitation.

"I won't let you harm him," Miri said flatly. "Not for some stupid test, and not for tradition. Quinnie is strong and perfect; you don't need to beat him up to know that. You'll take my word for it, is that understood?"
Thyra's gaze dropped to her.

Miri did not flinch. Her defiance was plain in the way her feet stayed rooted, in how her body leaned forward a fraction as if daring the taller woman to try. The size difference meant nothing to her. Quinlan could feel the protective, motherly intent rolling off her back.
Thyra's eyes shifted.
Luminara had stepped up as well, just a half step behind Miri. Her posture mirrored the same readiness. There was no bluff there either. If this turned violent, she would move without pause.
Just as they did when Dragnar tried to attack Quinlan for his own test, the two women were ready to throw down in order to protect their son.
For a long moment, Thyra said nothing.
Then her lips pulled into a wide grin.
"So," she said, voice rough, edged with gravel and wind-worn humor, "the two mother bears have finally found their cub, hm?"
She reached out and placed a broad hand on each of their shoulders at the same time.
"I'm happy for you two."
Miri stiffened in surprise. Luminara blinked, ears flicking back, then forward again as she processed the lack of threat.

Quinlan exhaled quietly. Based on how his mothers had reacted, Thyra clearly carried a reputation for being rough in both word and deed, just like Dragnar. She probably would've attacked him if not for his mothers, to measure his person or something like that. Thyra's attention returned to him.
"Your mothers are very important to me, child. If you ever make them cry, you'll have to deal with me."
Before Quinlan could respond, a sharp stomp echoed.
"Thyra!" Mearie snapped, foot hitting the stone path hard enough to draw attention. "Stop acting like you're my mother!"
Luminara scoffed beside her. "Mearie is one thing, but we're the same age. I don't need your protection."
Thyra looked at the elf, then grimaced. "You're so small and thin. You should put more meat on your bones."
Miri's scoff increased. "Are you ignoring me?!"
Thyra reached down without warning and patted Miri's hair, fingers brushing through it with casual familiarity. "Calm down, little one."
"!!" Miri's eyes went wide.
She slapped the hand away. "I'm not a baby anymore! I stopped being one millions of years ago!"
Thyra's expression softened as she looked down at her. "They grow up so fast," she muttered with a tired sigh.
Miri's face tightened. Her grip on the spear creaked.
Quinlan burst into a wide grin as he looked between them. "Wait. Don't tell me... Are you Miri's mother?"

Primordials were birthed by divine magic, from the governing bodies of the universe, the higher divinities. Thus, they had no biological mothers. Just like how Mearie and Luminara were his adoptive mothers, that was the form of relationship Quinlan meant.

Thyra turned her head toward him, expression plain and unembellished. "Miri? That's a good name, I approve. As for your question... She was a timid little girl. She would have perished without my protection. I remember her hiding behind me for years on end, clutching my clothes tightly, refusing to let go."
Quinlan shifted his gaze to Miri and raised an eyebrow questioningly.
Miri, in response, froze.

"Would you happen to be Thyra?" he asked and respectfully introduced himself.
"Greetings, my name is Quinlan, the newest primordial and the son of Luminara and Mearie."
He remembered the stories.
Malakar and Thyra.
The first human pair.
The foundation that was laid long before kingdoms learned to name themselves.
Despite it being Mearie who stayed on the Iskaris Continent, Thyra had come far earlier.
The woman standing before him was the true mother of humanity.
Almost all denizens of Iskaris descended from her and Malakar.
Thyra studied him for several heartbeats.
Then she stepped closer.
Only when she stood directly in front of him did Quinlan realize the full measure of it.
She was tall, extremely so.
Two meters (6'6") tall, to be exact, which meant she was standing eye to eye with Quinlan.
She was the first woman who matched his height since his transformation with the Primordial Breeding Physique he unlocked before boning Blossom right after saving her from her slave contract.
Miri stepped forward before Quinlan could shift his weight.
She planted herself between them, shoulders squared, chin lifted as she looked up at the towering woman in front of her.
Her fingers tightened around her spear, not raised, but ready.
Her stance carried no hesitation.
"I won't let you harm him," Miri said flatly.
"Not for some stupid test, and not for tradition.
Quinnie is strong and perfect; you don't need to beat him up to know that.
You'll take my word for it, is that understood?"
Thyra's gaze dropped to her.
Miri did not flinch.
Her defiance was plain in the way her feet stayed rooted, in how her body leaned forward a fraction as if daring the taller woman to try.
The size difference meant nothing to her.
Quinlan could feel the protective, motherly intent rolling off her back.
Thyra's eyes shifted.
Luminara had stepped up as well, just a half step behind Miri.
Her posture mirrored the same readiness.
There was no bluff there either.
If this turned violent, she would move without pause.
Just as they did when Dragnar tried to attack Quinlan for his own test, the two women were ready to throw down in order to protect their son.
For a long moment, Thyra said nothing.
Then her lips pulled into a wide grin.
"So," she said, voice rough, edged with gravel and wind-worn humor, "the two mother bears have finally found their cub, hm?"
She reached out and placed a broad hand on each of their shoulders at the same time.
"I'm happy for you two."
Miri stiffened in surprise.
Luminara blinked, ears flicking back, then forward again as she processed the lack of threat.
Quinlan exhaled quietly.
Based on how his mothers had reacted, Thyra clearly carried a reputation for being rough in both word and deed, just like Dragnar.
She probably would've attacked him if not for his mothers, to measure his person or something like that.
Thyra's attention returned to him.
"Your mothers are very important to me, child.
If you ever make them cry, you'll have to deal with me."
Before Quinlan could respond, a sharp stomp echoed.
"Thyra!" Mearie snapped, foot hitting the stone path hard enough to draw attention.
"Stop acting like you're my mother!"
Luminara scoffed beside her.
"Mearie is one thing, but we're the same age.
I don't need your protection."
Thyra looked at the elf, then grimaced.
"You're so small and thin.
You should put more meat on your bones."
Miri's scoff increased.
"Are you ignoring me?!"
Thyra reached down without warning and patted Miri's hair, fingers brushing through it with casual familiarity.
"Calm down, little one."
"!!" Miri's eyes went wide.
She slapped the hand away.
"I'm not a baby anymore!
I stopped being one millions of years ago!"
Thyra's expression softened as she looked down at her.
"They grow up so fast," she muttered with a tired sigh.
Miri's face tightened.
Her grip on the spear creaked.
Quinlan burst into a wide grin as he looked between them.
"Wait.
Don't tell me...
Are you Miri's mother?"
Primordials were birthed by divine magic, from the governing bodies of the universe, the higher divinities.
Thus, they had no biological mothers.
Just like how Mearie and Luminara were his adoptive mothers, that was the form of relationship Quinlan meant.
Thyra turned her head toward him, expression plain and unembellished.
"Miri?
That's a good name, I approve.
As for your question...
She was a timid little girl.
She would have perished without my protection.
I remember her hiding behind me for years on end, clutching my clothes tightly, refusing to let go."
Quinlan shifted his gaze to Miri and raised an eyebrow questioningly.
Miri, in response, froze.

chapters.title: Chapter 1394 New Faces
paragraphs: Miri, in response, froze. Then color crept into her cheeks. She looked away, ears and posture betraying her far faster than words ever could. "It's true," she admitted after a moment. "At least the part where she raised me."

She straightened, and her voice steadied as she continued. "We primordials are born with physically grown bodies, but while our brains are also fully formed, our minds need stimulus to settle, experience to grow. After conception, we're... wild. Primal. Some feel the urge to shed blood without reason. Some seek protection. Some want to mate. Some want to hide. It varies."
Her hand relaxed on the spear. "As time passes, our psyche develops. We grow into ourselves."
Quinlan listened, then nodded once. "Interesting."
Thyra studied him again, this time with open curiosity. "Speaking of," she said, brow lifting slightly, "Isn't your son too collected for a newborn?"
"Hehe!" Luminara declared at once, chest puffed out with pride. "Our Quinnie is a special boy!"
Miri nodded along, entirely earnest. "Very special."
Thyra's lips curved into a broad smile. The earlier edge softened into something warmer, her presence settling like a mountain at rest. "Well, I won't pry more. Good for you," she said simply.
Quinlan found that he liked this gentle giant... Though he didn't know if calling her gentle was justified based on the initial attitude of his mothers.
Nonetheless, just as with Dragnar, he was drawn to their personalities.
He glanced around the clearing. "Where's Dragnar?"
Luminara answered without hesitation. "He volunteered for Nyxara duty!"
Understanding came immediately.
Nyxara, the succubus who kept trying to mate with him at every opportunity. Dragnar was likely locked in constant combat just to keep her occupied.
Some trials, Quinlan decided, were crueler than others.
"So this is the child?"
The voice came from the edge of the clearing, calm and measured.
Quinlan turned.

Two figures were approaching side by side, their steps quiet despite the earth beneath their feet. Their features were unmistakably eastern, carrying a balance and sharpness that pulled at an old memory from another life. They reminded him of Japanese warriors from the history books on Earth.
Just a lot better looking.
The woman walked slightly ahead.

Her hair was dark, tied back with care, a few loose strands framing her face. Her features carried the same clean lines Ayame had, though aged into something more settled. Where Ayame still held a lot of sharpness, this woman carried patience instead. Her kimono was layered and practical, the fabric reinforced where needed, and at her hip rested a katana whose sheath bore no ornament.

The man beside her was broader through the shoulders, posture straight without stiffness. His gaze was steady, scanning the space without urgency. His katana sat at his left side, hand close but relaxed.
They both stopped a few steps away.
"He truly is a newborn. I can sense it..." the woman murmured. She retained her composed attitude, but Quinlan could sense some joy beneath it all. A new primordial being born was a joyous occasion.
The man nodded once. "Nice to meet you, kid. Let me know if you need some guidance. Malakar and Dragnar are not exactly what I'd call ideal male role models."
"I must agree," Malakar grumbled. "Tell your mothers to stop bothering me, Laddy. You have your male role model now."

Quinlan, ignoring the grumpy old man, stepped forward, mindful of his posture. He gave them the respect they deserved without bowing or groveling. "Greetings. My name is Quinlan, son of Luminara and Mearie."
The woman inclined her head with a tender smile. "Such a well-mannered baby. My name is Hanae."
The man sported an even bigger upward tug of his lips. "Just call me Uncle Zen."

Quinlan had to force back a ginger expression from emerging. Being treated like a baby was a hard pill to swallow. But at the same time, he understood where they were coming from. Not only were they literally millions of years older, but they were also much stronger and more experienced as well.
Quinlan's total age of mind was about forty, so even with those years counted, they still had every right to treat him as a kid.
That's why Quinlan kept his expression even. It took effort.

Mostly because Hanae was an extremely gorgeous woman, striking in a way that demanded attention without asking for it. He firmly refused to let his thoughts wander where they had no business going, especially because she seemed to be content next to the male primordial, Zen. He didn't know their exact relationship, as after all these years, most of the primordials, even those who were together on Thalorind, have separated. They couldn't sire children in this dimension, after all. All they could do here was fight for their sanity against the miserable passage of time, which most of them preferred to do alone.
All that is to say, not only was Hanae way out of his league for now, considering she was treating him like a literal baby, but Quinlan had no intentions to wreck a happy marriage either.
Hanae studied him openly. "Less than a year..." she said, as if confirming a measurement. "You stand tall and straight for one so young."
Zen smirked. "Impressive. How about a duel?"
Quinlan wasn't one to shy away. In fact, fighting such a mighty person was a great boon.
But...
"No, we're having a party first! The boys can have their fun later," Luminara pouted.
"I concur," Hanae responded with a nod, then narrowed her eyes at Zen. "Don't take the child away. I just met him."
"My bad, my bad..." Zen chuckled, raising both arms in surrender. It seemed most male primordials knew how to behave when confronted with the desires of the fairer gender.
That was when Quinlan met Zen's gaze.
There was no need for words. No nod either. Just a shared stillness, the faint pull of mutual intent settling between them like a promise deferred.
'Later.'
Both of them understood it at the same time.
Zen's mouth curved slightly. Quinlan allowed the smallest lift at the corner of his lips in return. Then they both looked away, expressions neutral, shoulders relaxed, very aware of the women nearby.
Angering them was a poor tactical decision.
The air shifted again.

A pop echoed at shoulder height, followed by a sharp smell of herbs and volatile reagents. A short figure appeared in a swirl of displaced mana, boots landing atop a stacked crate that had not existed a moment earlier. He wore a tailored coat layered with pockets, vials clinking faintly with every movement. A pair of thick glasses sat low on his nose, lenses tinted a faint green.
"Late, late, terribly late," the gnome muttered, rifling through a satchel without looking up. "Temporal calibration was off by three heartbeats. Unacceptable."
He paused, finally glancing around.
"Where is she?" he demanded. "The alchemist. I was told I'd be receiving an apprentice."
Quinlan looked toward Miri.

She straightened a little, hands folding together. "That would be Aurora. Thindlebrim is the male gnome primordial and the greatest alchemist among us. I thought she might learn something just by spending time near him. Even if he doesn't let her touch anything."

"No touching!!" Thindlebrim snapped instantly, jabbing a finger into the air. "Absolutely no touching. Only the worthy may lay hands on my tools, my vials, my notes, or my workspaces. Proximity is a privilege already."
He adjusted his glasses with a sniff, chin lifting.
Luminara leaned in slightly, peering past him. "Where's she? I expected her to be glued to your side."

chapters.title: Chapter 1395 Discovering New Races
paragraphs: Thindlebrim waved a dismissive hand. "That sentimental creature heard we'd have a new student and immediately began baking welcome cookies. Or cakes. Or some other inefficient use of perfectly good ingredients. She insisted it was important for morale."
He scoffed. "Utter nonsense."
Before Quinlan could respond, the clearing stirred again.

More figures stepped out from the paths, the crowd thickening with familiar and unfamiliar faces alike. Quinlan's gaze paused when he noticed a pair approaching together, their presence carrying a familiar elegance, yet something was different.

Their skin was dark, and their ears bore the same long taper as Luminara's, their features refined in the same elven way. But unlike the serenity of elves, he sensed a deeper animosity there, a generic tendency for violence that the elves lacked by nature.
"Dark elves?" Quinlan asked, honestly curious.
Miri yelped. "No, Quinnie, you can't call them that!"

The woman laughed softly, lifting a hand in greeting. Her white hair fell in a dark curtain down her back, eyes bright with amusement. "It's fine, Mearie. Babies will be babies. We look a bit like elves, and our skin is dark, so the mistake makes sense."
"I didn't know you'd grown so accepting," Luminara raised an eyebrow.
"Spending eternity staring at empty walls does that to you. I think I lost some of my edge."
Luminara grimaced with understanding.
The man beside her did not share her ease.
His eyes narrowed, shadows deepening around his feet as something heavy stirred in the space behind him. His voice carried a low edge when he spoke. "We are drows."

Quinlan inclined his head immediately. "My apologies. I made a mistake due to my ignorance. I'm currently stuck in the Continent of Iskaris, which means I have no access to information about your people... I won't repeat such a mistake."
The shadows stilled.
Both of them blinked, caught off guard. The woman tilted her head, studying him anew. The man's posture eased by a fraction, tension draining from his shoulders.
She glanced toward Luminara and Mearie and gave the pair a knowing wink. "Your parenting skills are improving even after all this time."
The male drow snorted quietly. "What kind of magic did you do? When I tried, my children bit me and then cried."
"That's why I did the parenting," the woman replied without missing a beat. Her smile seemed fake for a moment, losing some warmth. Quinlan sensed dissatisfaction there.
But then, the drow turned back to Quinlan and her previous warmth returned. "I'm Kiryssa. This is Vaelor."
Vaelor gave a short nod, arms crossing again, though the shadows no longer pressed so close.

Quinlan felt it then, the shape of the gathering settling into something warm and alive. Laughter drifted between old acquaintances. While the eyes were strictly on him, studying with immense curiosity, conversations began to spark. The weight he had expected from having to meet so many primordials never came.
He had braced for scrutiny. For judgment. For cold appraisal.
Instead, while some of them were most certainly eccentric, he found a warm welcome.

As he looked around, understanding followed. This celebration, or 'party' as his mothers had called it, had not been arranged solely for him. A new primordial was reason for those who had endured time in solitude to gather again, to speak, to remember what it meant to belong to something larger than themselves.
Quinlan let out a slow breath.
This was not just his party.
It was a family reunion.
The ground shifted, drumming. Something heavy was approaching.
Quinlan's head turned.
Far off, beyond the edge of the clearing and past the distant treeline, two shapes moved against the horizon. At first, they were silhouettes. Then scale settled in.
His eyes widened.
"...Giants?!" he asked, unable to keep the lift out of his voice.
"Hehe, yes," Luminara replied at once, pleased. "They are very gentle people."
Quinlan squinted.

Even from more than a mile away, the details were clear. The male was massive beyond reason, his frame wide enough that each step pressed shallow impressions into the land. Thick cords of muscle wrapped his legs, layered and defined like living stone. Beside him walked a female giant, slightly smaller, one hand raised as she spoke to him with sharp gestures.
The male suddenly stopped.
He bent one knee.
The female's arm shot out, palm slapping against his thigh as if to stop him. She shook her head, visibly scolding him.
He ignored her.
Muscles tightened. Even from this distance, Quinlan could see the way his legs bunched, power drawing inward. Then the giant crouched.
"Oh," Quinlan murmured.
The ground cracked outward in a wide ring as the giant pushed off.

The sound came a heartbeat later, a heavy thunder that rolled through the clearing. The giant's body lifted cleanly into the air, arcing upward with frightening speed, blotting out a stretch of sky as he sailed toward them.
Quinlan's breath caught. "Wait. Isn't this bad?"
The shape grew larger far too quickly.

"Idiot!" Miri's voice snapped, sharp enough to cut through the noise. She stepped forward, eyes blazing as she glared at the flying figure. "Hagnar! When will you learn that you're titans?! You'll destroy the village when you land!"
High above, the giant's limbs flailed in a sudden loss of confidence. His eyes went wide.
The voice that followed was the deepest Quinlan had ever heard, impossibly heavy, as if the air itself had to move aside for it.
"Sorry..." the giant muttered. "I was too excited..."
Miri pinched the bridge of her nose and exhaled. "Fine."
She planted her feet. Her body shifted into motion with practiced ease, spear sliding into her grip as she turned side-on. Her shoulders set. Her arm drew back.
The muscles along her back and arm tightened, power gathering in a way Quinlan recognized all too well. He had seen her fight. He knew exactly how strong she was.
For a moment, she looked less like a mother and more like a Valkyrie. She intended to shoot him out of the sky.
"Mother, wait," Quinlan said, stepping forward.
Miri paused, her arm locked in place just before release. She glanced back at him, brow lifting.
"Hm? What is it, Quinnie? Are you scared? Don't worry, Mommy will protect you."
"It's not that," Quinlan smiled, putting a hand on her throwing arm. "Let me try. I don't want you to skewer him."

"I don't think this is a good idea. Hagnar weighs more than some mountains, and he's flying toward us at a rapid pace. Let us take care of it, Quinnie. You can show us what a strong boy you became afterwards," Luminara spoke up with an extreme amount of motherly affection and protectiveness. While what she said might've seemed condescending at a first glance, the way she said it made it clear she only wanted to protect him.

But that was the exact thing. After being treated like a literal evil demon who was the worst thing to have happened to an entire kingdom, to now being treated like a newborn baby... The contrast was too stark for him to take easily.
"Mothers, you could trust your son just a tad bit more," Quinlan grinned while stepping forward. Mana gathered at his fingertips.

He knew that he was out of his league among these people. He knew that they likely had a way to get the giant out of the skies even without literally skewering him on a spear. These beings had many tools to do the job.

But while being treated like a kid was fine and all, especially when that meant being pampered by his mothers, he much preferred being treated with just a tad more respect. 'Is this what my Ayame calls primordial arrogance...?' Quinlan mused inwardly as he called upon his powers. 'Failing now will ensure I never drop the incompetent baby allegations...'

Beside him walked a female giant, slightly smaller, one hand raised as she spoke to him with sharp gestures.
The male suddenly stopped.
He bent one knee.
The female's arm shot out, palm slapping against his thigh as if to stop him.
She shook her head, visibly scolding him.
He ignored her.
Muscles tightened.
Even from this distance, Quinlan could see the way his legs bunched, power drawing inward.
Then the giant crouched.
"Oh," Quinlan murmured.
The ground cracked outward in a wide ring as the giant pushed off.
The sound came a heartbeat later, a heavy thunder that rolled through the clearing.
The giant's body lifted cleanly into the air, arcing upward with frightening speed, blotting out a stretch of sky as he sailed toward them.
Quinlan's breath caught.
"Wait.
Isn't this bad?"
The shape grew larger far too quickly.
"Idiot!" Miri's voice snapped, sharp enough to cut through the noise.
She stepped forward, eyes blazing as she glared at the flying figure.
"Hagnar!
When will you learn that you're titans?!
You'll destroy the village when you land!"
High above, the giant's limbs flailed in a sudden loss of confidence.
His eyes went wide.
The voice that followed was the deepest Quinlan had ever heard, impossibly heavy, as if the air itself had to move aside for it.
"Sorry..." the giant muttered.
"I was too excited..."
Miri pinched the bridge of her nose and exhaled.
"Fine."
She planted her feet.
Her body shifted into motion with practiced ease, spear sliding into her grip as she turned side-on.
Her shoulders set.
Her arm drew back.
The muscles along her back and arm tightened, power gathering in a way Quinlan recognized all too well.
He had seen her fight.
He knew exactly how strong she was.
For a moment, she looked less like a mother and more like a Valkyrie.
She intended to shoot him out of the sky.
"Mother, wait," Quinlan said, stepping forward.
Miri paused, her arm locked in place just before release.
She glanced back at him, brow lifting.
"Hm?
What is it, Quinnie?
Are you scared?
Don't worry, Mommy will protect you."
"It's not that," Quinlan smiled, putting a hand on her throwing arm.
"Let me try.
I don't want you to skewer him."
"I don't think this is a good idea.
Hagnar weighs more than some mountains, and he's flying toward us at a rapid pace.
Let us take care of it, Quinnie.
You can show us what a strong boy you became afterwards," Luminara spoke up with an extreme amount of motherly affection and protectiveness.
While what she said might've seemed condescending at a first glance, the way she said it made it clear she only wanted to protect him.
But that was the exact thing.
After being treated like a literal evil demon who was the worst thing to have happened to an entire kingdom, to now being treated like a newborn baby...
The contrast was too stark for him to take easily.
"Mothers, you could trust your son just a tad bit more," Quinlan grinned while stepping forward.
Mana gathered at his fingertips.
He knew that he was out of his league among these people.
He knew that they likely had a way to get the giant out of the skies even without literally skewering him on a spear.
These beings had many tools to do the job.

But while being treated like a kid was fine and all, especially when that meant being pampered by his mothers, he much preferred being treated with just a tad more respect. 'Is this what my Ayame calls primordial arrogance...?' Quinlan mused inwardly as he called upon his powers. 'Failing now will ensure I never drop the incompetent baby allegations...'

chapters.title: Chapter 1396 Extreme Mass
paragraphs: Quinlan felt it the moment he stepped forward.

Attention settled on him from every direction. Threads of interest brushed against his skin, old and patient presences taking stock. Many of them did not know what he was capable of. To most, he was simply Luminara's and Miri's adopted son, the late arrival, the curiosity.
He rolled his shoulders once and raised both arms.
Mana slid into place, clean and familiar.
Wind answered first.

The air thickened around his forearms, pressure building as he pushed outward. A rush rolled across the clearing, grass bending, loose fabric snapping. The force surged ahead in the form of a broad shove aimed at the incoming giant.
The wind struck Hagnar's massive form and... slipped.

It rippled along his skin, tugged at his hair, fluttered against his clothes. The man drifted through it without slowing, still hurtling toward the village with an expression of rising panic. "You'll need something much stronger..." he murmured, half begging.
"Oh, an elemental mage?" Kiryssa tilted her head, silver eyes narrowing with interest.
Hanae's eyes narrowed. "With those big muscles of his? I thought he'd be a fighter."
Zen shrugged. "It's manly to have big muscles. Mages can work out, too, you know? But..."
The eastern-featured pair's gaze lingered, slower this time. Hanae watched the way Quinlan stood, the set of his legs, the way his weight stayed centered even as he adjusted to the failed push.
"...He's a fighter, all right," she murmured. "A hybrid."
"That's rare for a primordial of such a low level," Zen commented. "I like it, very ambitious."
Miri's hand tightened around her spear shaft. Her jaw set as she tracked the useless wind with sharp eyes.
Lumi stood rigid beside her, fingers curled at her side, magic gathering unconsciously along her knuckles before she forced it back down. Her lips pressed thin.

Both mothers were extremely worried. Until now, Quinlan always took a backseat in the primordial realm, letting them do the fighting while he watched. While this wasn't a fight per se, it was still a major challenge.
And their son had stepped forward, intending to show his worth.
Naturally, seeing the fire in his eyes, both mothers were anxiously rooting for their son to succeed. No mother wanted to see their child fail.
Quinlan exhaled slowly. While he was surprised at the utterly zero effect his heavy push of wind had, he had known the wind would not be enough. It had been a test, nothing more.
"Okay," he muttered.
His stance widened. Mana sank deeper, heavier. The ground beneath his boots answered with a dull tremor.
Earth rose.
Stone tore free in rough slabs, chunks the size of wagons ripping upward in a staggered line. Dust burst outward as Quinlan swung his arms, hurling the mass skyward with blunt force.
The stones slammed into Hagnar's body in a staggered barrage.
They shattered.
Rock split and burst apart on impact, fragments spinning away like broken pottery. The giant grunted as pieces bounced off his chest and shoulders, barely deflected, his trajectory unchanged.
Quinlan watched the debris rain down.
"Is he really a giant? He's too big..."

Now that Hagnar was closer, Quinlan could guess his proportions with reliable accuracy. The man was around 100 meters (328') tall, full of muscles and adorned with heavy armor and, as if that wasn't enough, a giant warhammer hung on his back. Just the hammerhead itself was bigger than the more humble human peasant houses.
No wonder his spells had so little effect. Hagnar's bulk was just too massive.

Thyra answered before anyone else could. "I'm impressed. Your intuition is strong, child. Hagnar is a giant primordial, but that size isn't natural. He unlocked the Titanic Physique during his journeys, which reshaped his body, scaling it far beyond that of normal giants. Strength, mass, resilience, all of it was greatly increased. When it comes to Strength and Vitality, no one can match Hagnar. Save for perhaps Dragnar if he gets his Primordial Dread class's berserker boosts to reach their peak."
Quinlan's brow lifted a fraction.
So that's it.
Understanding clicked into place.
'Just like my Primordial Breeding Physique,' Quinlan mused inwardly.

After unlocking that ability, he had grown as well. His body had changed when it took root, density, vitality, and endurance all climbing steadily. But instead of runaway size, his path had split elsewhere.
Into a different kind of advantage.
[Blessed Seed]

A trait that let him empower those bound to him through intimacy, weaving strength and growth into the act itself. A gift that bolstered those around him rather than being restricted to his personal power strictly, one that turned connection into amplification.
Quinlan let out a quiet breath through his nose.
Yeah. He was very glad he'd gotten his instead.
Hagnar, for all his overwhelming presence, had only one possible partner. His primordial counterpart, who seemed to be only slightly shorter. Anyone else was simply incompatible.
Quinlan shuddered faintly at the thought.
To be locked out from his girls entirely...
That wasn't a blessing.
That was a curse.
However, Quinlan didn't have time to dwell on it.

Hagnar had jumped from far beyond the treeline, but distance meant little at that speed. The giant was still cutting through the sky with frightening velocity. The air pressure shifted. The shadows beneath him stretched and thickened.
Around Quinlan, subtle movements rippled through the gathering.
Feet adjusted. Hands loosened from restraints. Power gathered just beneath the surface.
They were giving him space. He could tell. But one more failure, and they would step in.
This was it.
Quinlan closed his eyes.
He didn't separate it this time. Didn't reach for one element and then another. He drew everything in at once.

Wind wrapped tight around his frame. Earth answered in his bones, weight and stability anchoring his balance. Heat rolled through his muscles, sharpening motion, driving force forward. Water followed, condensing it all, keeping it controlled.
Mana flooded his limbs.
So did memory.
Hours spent breaking his body down and building it back up. Strikes drilled until form held under exhaustion. Impact trained not to look pretty, only to work.
His eyes snapped open.
"[Elemental Stance: Flame]."
His body wrapped in heat as he called upon his elemental stance that boosted his Strength.

chapters.title: Chapter 1397 A Humbling Experience
paragraphs: The ground beneath him fractured as he launched upward.

Wind tore him from the earth, spiraling tight instead of spreading wide. He cut through the rising dust and shattered stone, body angled forward, knee drawn in. The giant loomed ahead, chest broad as a cliff face, eyes widening as Quinlan closed the gap.
Too small. Too late.
That was the thought on Hagnar's face.
Then Quinlan struck.
His heel drove into the center of the giant's chest, all four elements compressed into a single point. The impact rang out dull and heavy, more felt than heard. No cry of pain followed. No recoil.
But Hagnar's momentum shifted.
Just enough.

The arc of his fall bent downward, no longer aimed for the heart of the village. The two of them fell together, and Hagnar's massive arms began sweeping through the air in broad, panicked arcs. The motion pushed against the wind itself, clumsy but purposeful, forcing his bulk to rotate beneath Quinlan.
"Don't worry," the giant said, voice booming yet oddly careful, as if he were afraid of hurting him with his loud voice alone. "I've got you."
The world tilted.

Hagnar twisted his body mid-fall and took the descent on his back, armor plates scraping and screaming against the rushing air. Quinlan dropped the last stretch straight down, momentum carrying him hard into the giant's armored belly.
He could have flown.
The thought flickered through his mind as the distance closed fast. Wind was already coiled around him. He could have corrected it, softened it, and taken control.
But he didn't.
There was something in the way Hagnar moved, in the deliberate effort to put himself underneath Quinlan, that made him stop. And, if he was honest, Quinlan was curious to see how this would end.
So he let it happen.
The impact came like the world folding inward.
Hagnar hit first.

The ground failed beneath him, earth collapsing into a vast bowl as his body slammed down. Soil, stone, and shattered bedrock surged outward in a violent ring. Trees near the edge bent and snapped. Dust rolled skyward in a thick column.
Quinlan struck a breath later.
Not gently.
His body bounced once against the giant's armor before settling, the shock tearing a sharp grunt from his throat. Pain flared along his ribs and sides as the force rattled through him.
Giants were not delicate creatures.
'Elephants in a porcelain shop,' Quinlan thought, a phrase dragged up from a life in a different world.
He lay there for a moment, staring up at the sky through drifting dust, breath forced shallow by the ache in his torso.
'Flying myself would've been so much better,' he sighed inwardly.
Below him, Hagnar let out a long laugh, the sound rolling through the crater like distant thunder, careful not to move too much.
"Thank you, child. You're a kind person," Hagnar boomed with his deep voice. "Let me take a better look at you."
Hagnar shifted beneath him.

The motion started small, a subtle roll through armor and muscle, then turned into something far more felt. The giant drew a deep breath, chest and belly expanding outward as if he were bracing for effort.
Quinlan barely had time to register the change.
Hagnar pushed.

The armored belly beneath Quinlan surged upward with absurd force, launching him cleanly off the giant's body. Air tore past him as he shot skyward, limbs flaring on instinct as he spun once, twice. Then many more times as he ragdolled in the air, resigning to just letting this absurd event run its course.
A shadow overtook him.

Two fingers closed around his torso with startling precision. Thick as tree trunks, warm with life, they pinched him gently enough to avoid harm while making escape a distant concept. His ascent stopped at once.
Hagnar lifted him closer, squinting with curiosity as he rotated Quinlan slowly between his fingers, turning him left and right like an interesting figurine.
Quinlan looked down.
The crater beneath them stretched wide. The scale settled in all at once.
Minutes ago, he had been a threat.
The menace of Thalorind. The one who tore through cities, cut down elite armies, and forced historical noble lineages into extinction.
Now he was launched into the air by a belly push and caught between two damned fingers.
A quiet, bitter humor crept in.
He had been getting ahead of himself. This was a much-needed slap of reality, telling Quinlan he wasn't the end-all be-all. There were creatures like this out there, too.

Hagnar turned him once more, careful and unhurried. "You should not be sad about being weak, child. What matters is that you are very brave. You can increase your levels, but increasing bravery is a tough thing to do."
"... Thanks," Quinlan grunted gingerly. He was feeling smaller by the minute.
Hagnar nodded, satisfied. "You will grow very strong someday. Perhaps then you can stop me properly."
Quinlan's mouth twitched. "I'll work on that."
The giant smiled, broad and earnest, entirely unaware of the extreme ego-crushing nature of his words.
"Good," he reached up with a third finger and patted his head. Synchra flared to protect her master, lest this gentle giant accidentally crush his skull.

"..." Quinlan didn't even know what to say. He was close to shedding a few tears as he let the giant pet his head. Hagnar was too kind a soul for Quinlan to begin hurling insults and demanding to be released.
Quinlan had to remind himself that to this giant, he was just a newborn primordial, who should act a lot more wild and childish than he did.
He allowed himself to keep it together until a shadow fell across Hagnar's hand.
Two much smaller figures landed atop it with enough force to make even the giant blink.
Miri was already moving.

She strode across the back of Hagnar's hand and planted her boots between his fingers, driving her spear haft down hard enough that it rang against his armor. "Stop this!" she hissed, eyes sharp and bright. "Put Quinnie down."

Luminara was beside her an instant later, hands gripping Quinlan's shoulders through the gap between those enormous fingers. Her voice was tight, pressed flat with worry. "That's enough. You're making Quinnie feel bad!"
Hagnar's eyes widened with shock.

chapters.title: Chapter 1398 Child Among Adults
paragraphs: Hagnar's eyes widened with shock.
He looked from their faces to Quinlan, then back again, brow furrowing in confusion. "I was being gentle," he said slowly.
Miri didn't answer. She pried his fingers apart with raw force, joints protesting as she forced them open just enough.
"Release," she demanded.
Hagnar obeyed at once.
Quinlan dropped.

Luminara caught him mid-fall, arms wrapping around his back as Miri pulled him in from the other side. They hit the ground together, knees bending to take the impact, and then they were holding him so tightly he could barely breathe, hugging him from both sides.
"You did amazing, Quinnie!" Luminara chirped at once, hands sliding up his arms, over his shoulders, as if checking him piece by piece. "Your mothers are beyond impressed!"
"So strong," Miri added, voice fierce and proud. She pressed her forehead to his temple. "Did you see that? You moved him. You stopped him."
Quinlan didn't answer.
He stared past them.
Around the edge of the crater, the other primordials watched in silence. No tension lingered. No alarm. Just soft smiles. A few nods. The kind given to children who had done well.
Kiryssa's lips curved in quiet approval. Hanae inclined her head. Even Zen looked faintly amused.
Not impressed.
Pleased.
The realization settled heavily in his chest.
He had leapt. Struck. Burned mana and body alike to force a result. In his mind, he had stood up among monsters and proven something.
To them, it had been a moment.
A clever display. A neat party trick at a gathering meant to welcome family.
His mothers pulled back just enough to look at him.
Their eyes shone.
Pure awe. Unfiltered pride. The kind that saw past scale, past outcome, and focused only on effort.
And somehow, that made it worse.
He felt like a kid who displayed his piano skills at a family gathering. His mothers were impressed, sparkly-eyed, while the other relatives looked on gently and clapped.
Hagnar's voice rumbled above them, careful now. "You have good mothers. They care for you very much."
Quinlan swallowed.
He nodded once, forcing a small breath through tight ribs. "Yeah," he said quietly.
"We love you so much, Quinnie!!" Miri squeezed him again. Luminara did the same.
Quinlan stayed where he was, held between them, feeling smaller than he had in a long time.
Unlike him, Hagnar began to move his limbs, attempting to rise from the ground.
It started with a shift of his shoulders, armor plates grinding as he planted one massive hand against the crater wall. The ground groaned in protest as his weight rolled forward.
Then the sky darkened.
A shadow that somehow felt far larger than his own swept across the clearing, followed by a sharp drop in pressure that made loose dust lift from the ground.
Quinlan felt it a heartbeat before it happened.
A colossal hand came down from above and smacked the back of Hagnar's head.
The sound was not a crack. It was not a boom.
It was a deep, concussive thoom that punched through the air and into the bones, a noise that flattened grass and rattled teeth. Hagnar's eyes went wide as his balance vanished entirely.
He faceplanted.

A towering figure landed beside him with arms crossed and a posture that radiated exhaustion.

She was a giant primordial as well, nearly his size, though slimmer in build. Her armor was lighter, layered plates shaped for movement rather than brute endurance. Long hair was bound back in a thick braid that swung as she leaned forward.

"You're unbelievable," she snapped, voice echoing across the clearing. "I told you. I've told you so. Many. Times. Do not jump when you see the child! Yet what do you do as soon as you see the child?!"
Hagnar groaned. "Jump..."
"Exactly! What do you have to say for yourself?!" she shot back. "N-nothing..." Hagnar spoke into the earth.
She planted one boot on the edge of the crater and leaned down, hands on her knees, glaring at the back of his head. "Every time it's the same. Act first, think never."
"I'll do better..."

She straightened and dragged a hand down her face, then exhaled slowly. "Haaah..." Turning toward the gathering, she stepped forward and bowed deeply. Deep enough that the ground creaked beneath the shift in her weight.

"My sincere apologies, everyone..." she said, voice steady now, edged with weariness rather than anger. Then she looked at Quinlan in particular. "I am Hyrmara, female giant primordial. And this," she jerked a thumb back at the crater, "is my husband, Hagnar."
Hagnar lifted one hand weakly in greeting without getting up. "Hello."
Hyrmara continued, "I am supposed to be his partner, but most days, I feel more like the caretaker of a horribly overgrown child."
Hagnar muttered something unintelligible.
She shot him a look sharp enough to silence him completely.
Quinlan let out a slow breath.
The tight knot in his chest finally loosened. It was time to stop feeling pity for himself.
He slipped one arm around Luminara's waist, the other around Miri's, pulling them both in. Their bodies pressed warmly against his sides.
"It's a pleasure to meet you," he said, voice calm again as he looked up at the towering woman. "I am Quinlan, son of these two wonderful women."
Hearing the way he introduced himself, Lumi beamed so brightly it was almost blinding, while Miri grinned, chin lifting with pride as she leaned into his side.
Hyrmara studied him for a moment, then nodded once. "I'm happy for you two. He seems like a good child."
"I know, right?!" the two women cheered instantly. Quinlan glanced around the clearing. The gathered primordials stood relaxed now, conversations murmuring softly, the tension fully gone.
"Is everyone here?" he asked.

Luminara nodded. "Everyone who was invited," she said. "There are other primordials like the vampires and the fey, among others. But they aren't our friends. We only invited those we trust to behave themselves around our son."
Quinlan nodded in understanding.
Then he smiled.
"Shall I introduce my girls then?"
Both mothers squealed at once, grabbing him tighter from either side.
Their voices rang across the clearing.
The gathered primordials turned, interest sparking anew.
It was time to finally bring the girls out of his soul realm.

chapters.title: Chapter 1399 Sisterly Bonding
paragraphs: Inside Quinlan's soul realm, the air was still.

The land spread out in gentle rises and shallow clearings, grass soft underfoot, the sky fixed in a quiet, pale glow. At its heart stood a single tree, small compared to Rosie's much vaster domain, its trunk smooth and pale, its leaves faintly luminous. Roots curled protectively around the ground beneath it, forming a natural seat where a small figure waited.

Mimi stood there, blue skin bright against the muted greens, hands clasped in front of her chest. The other girls had gathered around without prompting, forming a loose circle, intending to chat the time away until Quinlan called for them.
Serika hovered at the edge. For a long moment, she only watched. Mimi tilted her head, large eyes tracking her with open curiosity, and still no sign of recognition from their long past.
She was, after all, the dryad born from Serika's dead sister's soul.
Serika took a breath and stepped forward.
The moment she was close enough, Mimi's face changed abruptly, lighting up. The little girl looked as though she had made a decision.

She bounced on her toes, then jumped, arms flinging wide. Serika barely had time to react before the small body collided gently with her chest, little hands grabbing at her cheeks as Mimi pressed her face against Serika's.
"You're back!" Mimi chirped, voice bright and needy. Her arms tightened, small fingers curling into Serika's hair as if afraid she might disappear.
Serika froze. "W-what?"

Then her arms came up, slow at first, then firm. She held the girl close, one hand bracing Mimi's back, the other cupping the back of her head. Her jaw tightened. Her breath hitched. Moisture gathered at the corners of her eyes despite her effort to keep steady.
Mimi had no idea.

The thought cut deep and soft all at once. The girl she had known for hundreds of years had lost all memory of that life. There was no shared past in Mimi's mind. No sisters. No nights spent curled together for warmth.
Only this pull. This feeling.
Mimi nuzzled closer, pressing her forehead against Serika's, her little hands sliding up to hold her face. "I missed you," she said simply, as if it explained everything.

Serika let out a breath she hadn't realized she was holding. Her fingers trembled as they brushed along Mimi's hair, smoothing it back again and again. Her eyes burned. Tears slipped free and tracked down her cheeks, soaking into the girl's hair.
Time passed.

No one interrupted. The others watched quietly as Serika lowered herself to sit, with Mimi still clinging to her. The dryad hummed softly, content, while Serika pressed her face into the girl's shoulder and breathed until the tightness eased.
Aurora was the one who finally spoke, her voice careful. "What happened, Mimi? Did you regain your memories?"
Mimi shifted, lifting her head to look around. She shook her head, hair bouncing. "No..." Serika's hand stilled for a moment, then resumed its gentle motion.

Mimi kept going, voice animated. "When the scary woman came and broke into the place, Mimi fought really hard. Mimi was very scared." She puffed her chest slightly at that, then softened. "After, Mimi slept a lot. Scary uncle helped Mimi wake up."
Vex and Ayame had to fight back laughter from erupting. Mimi was akin to the guardian and administrator of Quinlan's soul realm. And such a person called him a scary uncle...?

Unaware, Mimi's gaze drifted up to Serika's face. "While sleeping, Mimi thought about stuff. About how big sister Serika always stayed nearby, even when Mimi didn't remember her." She smiled, small and earnest. "It must've been hard, right...?"
Serika couldn't respond; her throat was too tight. "Mimi really missed you. A whole lot." Her fingers tightened against Serika's cheeks. "Sorry for not remembering."

Serika swallowed. Her voice came out low and steady only through effort. "You have nothing to apologize for." She rested her forehead against Mimi's hair and kissed the top of her head once. "You're here. That's enough."
Mimi beamed and hugged her again, squeezing with all her small strength.
Kitsara stepped closer and patted Serika's shoulder, her expression warm. "I'm happy for you," she said.
Lucille crossed her arms, a wide grin on her face. "Yeah. Good for you, Seri."
Serika looked up at them, eyes red, cheeks damp. She laughed softly and nodded. "Thank you, guys."
The others smiled back.

They watched a woman who usually carried herself with calm certainty and hard edges sit on the grass, holding a small blue girl like she was the most precious thing in the world. Her firm muscles were still there. Her posture still strong. But her hands shook just a little as she held on, and her expression was open in a way none of them saw often.

"But wait..." Serika drew in a sharp breath, eyes widening as a thought caught up to her. "Why now? I've already visited you many times since that nasty bitc— I mean, woman invaded the realm. You didn't say anything then."
Mimi stiffened.

Her eyes went wide, hands loosening their grip. She pulled back from the hug with a small gasp, then hesitated before carefully stepping onto Serika's open palm. The scale difference made her movements extremely delicate. She stood there with her feet close together, shoulders slightly hunched.
Her fingers found the frilled edge of her little dress. She pinched the fabric, rubbing it back and forth while staring at her toes.
"Because I was shy," she admitted softly. "Mimi had to gather bravery first."
She peeked up.
The look was devastating. Huge eyes, glossy and uncertain, framed by a hopeful tilt of her head. "Are you disappointed? Angry?"
"!" Serika didn't answer. Not verbally, at least.
She simply lifted her other hand and pulled Mimi in again, pressing the small body back against her. The motion was firm and immediate, leaving no space for doubt.
Mimi squeaked, then laughed, the sound light and bubbling as she wrapped her arms around Serika once more.

Ayame watched the scene with a flat expression, arms crossed. After a moment, she spoke. "Look at this. Two sisters reconnecting even through death. Still tied together after lost memories and a changed race." Her gaze drifted away. "And here I am, sold into slavery by my own sister. Life has a sense of humor."

Vex's mouth curved into a grin. "Kaede might be a..." Serika sent her a gaze, forbidding the Hexwitch from cursing. She gingerly continued with the family-friendly version. "Questionably desired sister, but aren't you forgetting something?"
Ayame glanced at her. "Hm?"
"You have a second sister, Miss Samurai Babe."
Ayame's eyes narrowed at once. "Only that arrogant guy gets to use dumb monikers on me. Understood?"
Vex snapped a playful salute. "Crystal."
Ayame's glare eased. She exhaled slowly. "Black Fang, huh..."
Lucille perked up. "Yeah. You could try reconnecting with her." She tilted her head. "Or connecting, I suppose. There isn't much to rebuild."
Ayame hesitated. "I think she's a decent woman underneath it all. But it's hard."
"Yeah..." several voices agreed quietly.
"Quin decided on a near impossible challenge, huh?" Kaelira asked with a little smile. The elf was already informed of some must-know harem gossip.

"Nothing is impossible for Master!" Blossom declared at once, chest puffed out, fists clenched at her sides. Her tail swished with certainty. "If Master thinks he can conquer Lady Black Fang's ice-cold heart, then he can! Blossom knows!"
The others laughed softly as the blonde dogkin beamed, utterly convinced.

"Never change, Blossom..." Aurora giggled fondly, liking how the dogkin remained still the same turbo-loyal girl she knew her to be from all those months ago. As the girls continued their chatter, waiting for Quinlan's call, something else was also happening in the soul realm.

chapters.title: Chapter 1400 Ancient Ladies
paragraphs: Beyond the clearing where the others waited, the soul realm stretched into low hills and open ground, quiet and unclaimed. Two figures walked there at an unhurried pace.

Light slid across skin marked by history. Orianna's floral tattoos traced along her shoulders and down her arms, inked petals and winding stems catching the pale glow as she moved. Beside her, Black Fang's purple, serpentine markings followed the lines of her body in darker curves, coiling over her back and thighs. Every step set muscle in motion beneath them. They looked built for battle and long nights, bodies honed rather than aged, presence heavy with years lived hard.
Orianna let out a slow breath. "I feel so out of place... Like a tagalong who wandered in by accident. Is it really fine for me to be here?"
Black Fang kept her gaze forward. "The feeling is mutual."
Orianna shot her a look. "Even you?"
"I am currently realm hopping," Black Fang replied, tone flat, as if that alone covered everything.
It did.

Orianna nodded once. "Right. After being stuck to Iskaris for four centuries, we leave by diving into the trunk of a tree and end up inside the mind of a man who keeps trying to bone you at any cost."
Black Fang's head turned just enough for a side glance to cut across Orianna, sharp and dangerous.
Orianna did not pull any statements back. She rolled her shoulders and sighed. "I was out cold for a short while, yet it feels like I missed centuries."
"I stayed conscious and still feel the same. This is... Plain absurd." The Venomborne Terror admitted with a difficult expression.
"That it is," Orianna nodded.
They walked on for a few steps, boots brushing through grass. The quiet pressed in around them.
Orianna huffed another breath, the sound closer to a tired laugh. "Listen to us. We sound like old women."
Black Fang's mouth twitched and quoted Quinlan, "We are 'ancient ladies,' after all..." Orianna paused where she was. "He really did say that, didn't he? The galls on that guy..."
"I thought I understood how this life of mine would go," Orianna went on. "I thought the road ahead was mapped. But everything has been turned sideways."
Orianna's steps slowed. Her gaze drifted ahead, unfocused, then tipped slightly upward as if she were looking past the hills and into an older scene.

"I remember back when he was just a weak rookie trying to win the Vesper Phenom competition. All elbows and bravado. Now look at him. Destroying cities. Eviscerating battalions. Dragging people across realms like it is a change of clothes. All within a few months."
Black Fang's pace did not change. The corner of her mouth lifted, just barely. "Back then, he flirted with Vex in public. Constantly."
Orianna's eyes widened, then lit. "Oh yeah! I remember now." She chuckled brightly. "Future Hubby. Future Wifey. They kept calling each other that. So corny."

She turned her head, grin widening as she studied Black Fang's profile. "And now he is trying to get into your pants. A woman with even more emotional baggage by a long mile. A woman who, once again, can snap his neck." Her grin turned sly. "I am starting to see a pattern. That man has a very acquired taste."
Black Fang stopped.
Her head turned fully this time. The glance that followed carried real weight, sharp enough to make Orianna nearly take on a defensive formation.
"Are you saying," Black Fang asked, voice low and even, "that I do not deserve to be courted?"

Orianna froze for half a breath. Then she burst out laughing, bending forward as she slapped a hand against Black Fang's shoulder. "Look at you! Twisting what I said to fit your agenda. You are starting to act like a proper woman now. Congratulations."
Black Fang swiped Orianna's hand away with a short, controlled motion. A small shadow cut across the pale light.
"Rosie agrees!" a bright voice declared from above. "Miss Black Fang deserves to be courted!"
Something green and fast dropped from the sky and landed squarely on Black Fang's shoulders with a soft thump. Small arms wrapped around her head for balance.
"So she should go on romantic dates with Daddy and let him charm her!"
Black Fang stiffened.
Her shoulders drew tight. One hand lifted, then stopped halfway, fingers curling. Her jaw set, eyes forward, posture rigid in a way Orianna had only seen before combat.

It wasn't that Black Fang didn't sense Rosie's descent... She could've dodged. But she trusted the girl. However, she never expected Rosie to sit where she did. The Venomborne Terror felt very uncomfortable right now. She's never allowed anyone to touch her in such a way, from behind at that.
Her survival instincts, honed through several lifetimes of extreme brutality, screamed at her to yank the girl off and cut her apart.
"Uh... Rosie," Orianna said carefully, one brow lifting. "I am not sure that is a safe spot. Why don't you come over to me?"
Rosie patted Black Fang's head, completely at ease. "No need. Miss Black Fang is a very nice, friendly ancient lady!"
Black Fang's expression shifted.
The discomfort drained away, replaced by something colder. Still. Quiet. The look of a predator deciding how much effort a kill required.
"Hehehe!" Rosie vanished, giggling as she shot upward and then dropped neatly onto Orianna's shoulders instead.
Orianna barely flinched.
"You are playing dangerous games, young lady," she murmured, a small smile tugging at her mouth. "Where were you?"
"Surveying the lands!" Rosie chirped, peering around from her perch.

"I see," Orianna said, nodding once. Then she added, "So we're about to meet those people, huh? Our progenitors..." "Yes! Grandmommy Lumi and Miri!" Rosie chirped with utmost excitement, her voice ringing out across the quiet hills. "Rosie heard so many tales of them and their giant bosom! She can't wait to be enveloped by all that motherly warmth! Daddy can't monopolize it all to himself, Rosie plans to challenge his dominion over them!!!"

As she spoke, the girl began making frantic, grabbing motions with her small hands, her fingers curling and uncurling in the air with pure, unadulterated excitement. She leaned forward over Orianna's head, her face flushed with the kind of heat usually reserved for a warrior entering a frenzy, but fueled by the singular desire to be pampered.
"Truly his child..." Black Fang murmured dryly. "What kind of nonsense is he teaching his newly born daughter?"
"Of course Rosie is his child! Rosie and Daddy are the best mommy milker connoisseurs in the whole universe!"

"A what...?" Orianna gasped. The use of language, originating directly from Quinlan's mouth, meaning it was Earth slang, sounded all too alien. But the Flower Queen didn't exactly need an explanation to understand the gist of it.
"...You're way too unhinged," Orianna giggled. She adjusted Rosie's legs, feeling the girl's sheer vibrating energy through her shoulders.

"This is what happens when a baby listens to an eccentric man like him talk nonsense from the moment of their birth..." Black Fang whispered under her breath, her eyes fixed firmly on the horizon, as if looking away might make the conversation disappear.
"How big are we talking?" Orianna asked curiously. Her own sense of propriety was clearly beginning to crumble under the weight of the absurdity.

"Ginormous!" Rosie chirped. She let go of Orianna's head to make massive, sweeping circles in the air with her arms, nearly toppling backward in her fervor. "They're primordial mommies! The most motherly mommies among the people who birthed all mortals of Thalorind! Of course, they will be extremely voluptuous!! It only makes sense!"

"That big...?" Orianna murmured with a hand coming up to her own chin in thought. "I get the human primordial, but aren't elves lithe creatures? I know they can have normal-sized curves, but they tend to be rather slim, perfect for navigating thick forests. I thought their progenitor would resemble that image."

"Not my Grandmommy!" Rosie puffed, crossing her arms with a look of supreme authority. Before the unhinged conversation could continue, all of a sudden, a deep voice boomed across the realm. "Ladies... It's time. Gather around."
"Finally!!!" Rosie instantly jumped to her feet and zoomed off at breakneck speed.
"This girl..." Orianna shook her head, smiling fondly. Then, together with Black Fang, the two ancient ladies made their way back to where the group gathered.

Light slid across skin marked by history.

Beside her, Black Fang's purple, serpentine markings followed the lines of her body in darker curves, coiling over her back and thighs.
Every step set muscle in motion beneath them.
They looked built for battle and long nights, bodies honed rather than aged, presence heavy with years lived hard.
Orianna let out a slow breath.
